title.en: Volume 134 Biographies 84: Ma Sui, Hun Jian

sentences.zh: 趙憬趙憬，字退翁，天水隴西人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Jing—Zhao Jing, style name Tuiweng, was a native of Longxi in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jing, whose courtesy name was Tuiweng, was from Longxi in Tianshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 總章中吏部侍郎、同東西臺三品仁本之曾孫。

translations.literal: He was the great-grandson of Renben, who in the Zongzhang era had been Vice Minister of Personnel and a third-rank official at both the Eastern and Western Terraces.
translations.idiomatic: He was the great-grandson of Renben, who under Emperor Gaozong had served as vice minister of personnel and as a third-rank official at both court secretariats.

sentences.zh: 祖諠歷左司郎中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chan had served in succession as Director of the Left Department.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chan had served as director in the left secretariat department.

sentences.zh: 父道先，洪州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His father Daoxian was Recording Secretary in Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daoxian had been a recording secretary in Hong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 憬少好學，誌行修潔，不求聞達。

translations.literal: Jing from youth loved learning; his aims and conduct were cultivated and pure, and he did not seek renown.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhao Jing loved learning; his conduct was earnest and scrupulous, and he sought no fame.

sentences.zh: 寶應中，玄宗、肅宗梓宮未祔，有司議山陵制度。

translations.literal: In the Baoying era, the coffins of Emperors Xuanzong and Suzong had not yet been placed together, and the relevant offices debated the regulations for the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoying reign (762–763), with the coffins of Emperors Xuanzong and Suzong still not interred together, the responsible offices debated tomb and mourning regulations.

sentences.zh: 時西蕃入寇，天下饑饉，憬以褐衣上疏，宜遵儉制，時人稱之。

translations.literal: At that time the Western Tubo invaded and famine spread across the realm; Jing submitted a memorial in commoner's garb urging adherence to frugal regulations, and people of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: With Tibet invading and famine wracking the empire, Jing submitted a memorial while dressed as a commoner, arguing for austere observances; contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 後連為州從事，試江夏尉。

translations.literal: Later he served in succession as a prefectural aide and was tried out as magistrate of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in succession as a prefectural aide and was appointed acting magistrate of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 累遷監察御史，隨牒籓府，歷殿中侍御史、太子舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted in turn to supervisory censor, followed postings to a princely establishment, and served as palace censor and as attendant in the Heir Apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to supervisory censor, took assignments with a princely establishment, and served as palace censor and as attendant in the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 居母憂，哀毀幾絕。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his mother, his grief and self-abasement nearly cost him his life.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his mother, his grief was so extreme that he nearly died from it.

sentences.zh: 服除，建中初，擢授水部員外郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, at the beginning of the Jianzhong era he was selected and appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Works for Water Conservancy.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended, in the early Jianzhong period (780–783) he was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Works' waterworks bureau.

sentences.zh: 未拜，會湖南觀察使李承請為副使、檢校工部郎中，充職。

translations.literal: Before he could take office, the Hunan observation commissioner Li Cheng requested him as deputy commissioner and as acting Director in the Ministry of Works, and he filled the post.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume that post, Hunan observation commissioner Li Cheng asked that he serve as deputy commissioner and acting director in the Ministry of Works, and he took up the assignment.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，承卒，遂知留後事。

translations.literal: After more than a year Cheng died, and Jing then took charge of the acting commissioner's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year Li Cheng died, and Jing thereupon managed the post as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋授潭州刺史、兼御史中丞、湖南觀察使，仍賜金紫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Prefect of Tanzhou, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief and Hunan observation commissioner, and was also granted the gold-and-purple insignia.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Tanzhou, concurrently vice censor-in-chief and Hunan observation commissioner, and was also granted the gold-and-purple regalia of high rank.

sentences.zh: 居二歲，受代歸京師，闔門靜居，不與人交。

translations.literal: After two years he was relieved and returned to the capital; he shut his gates and lived quietly, associating with no one.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was relieved and returned to the capital, where he kept to his household in seclusion and associated with almost no one.

sentences.zh: 久之，特召對於別殿。

translations.literal: After a long while he was specially summoned for an audience in a side hall.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was specially summoned for an audience in a side hall of the palace.

sentences.zh: 憬多學問，有辭辯，敷奏稱旨，上悅，拜給事中。

translations.literal: Jing was broadly learned and eloquent; his presentations pleased the emperor, who was delighted and appointed him Gentleman Attendant at the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jing was learned and articulate; his presentations pleased the throne, and the emperor appointed him gentleman attendant at the gate.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年，回紇請結和親。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan the Uyghurs requested a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In 788 the Uyghurs sought a marriage alliance with the court.

sentences.zh: 詔以鹹安公主降回紇，命檢校右僕射關播充使。

translations.literal: An edict gave Princess Xian'an in marriage to the Uyghurs and ordered the acting Right Vice Director Guan Bo to serve as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The court decreed that Princess Xian'an be given in marriage to the Uyghurs and appointed acting right vice director Guan Bo chief envoy.

sentences.zh: 憬以本官兼御史中丞為副。

translations.literal: Jing served as deputy with his current office, concurrently as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Jing served as deputy envoy in his current post, concurrently as vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 前後使回紇者，多私賫繒絮，蕃中市馬回以規利。

translations.literal: Envoys to the Uyghurs before and after often privately carried silk and cotton to trade for horses in the foreign markets on the return journey for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Previous and later envoys to the Uyghurs often carried private loads of silk and cotton, buying horses in the frontier markets on the return trip for personal profit.

sentences.zh: 憬一無所市，人嘆美之。

translations.literal: Jing made no purchases whatsoever, and people sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Jing made no private purchases at all, and people praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 使還，遷尚書左丞，綱轄省務，清勤奉職。

translations.literal: On his return from the mission he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, directing the ministry's affairs with purity and diligence in service.
translations.idiomatic: After the mission he was promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, where he oversaw ministry business with scrupulous diligence.

sentences.zh: 竇參為宰相，惡其能，請出為同州刺史，上不從。

translations.literal: When Dou Can served as chief minister he resented Jing's ability and requested that he be sent out as Prefect of Tongzhou; the emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Dou Can, resenting Jing's talent, asked that he be sent out as prefect of Tongzhou, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，竇參罷黜，憬與陸贄並拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year Dou Can was dismissed; Jing and Lu Zhi were both appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors with concurrent authority at the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 792 Dou Can was removed from office; Zhao Jing and Lu Zhi were both appointed vice director of the Secretariat and grand councilors.

sentences.zh: 憬深於理道，常言：「為政之本，在於選賢能，務節儉，薄賦斂，寬刑罰。

translations.literal: Jing was deeply versed in the principles of governance and often said: "The root of governing lies in selecting the worthy and able, striving for frugality, lightening taxes and levies, and moderating punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was deeply versed in statecraft and often said, "The foundation of government lies in choosing worthy officials, practicing frugality, lightening taxes, and moderating punishments.

sentences.zh: 」對揚之際，必以此為言，乃獻《審官六議》曰：

translations.literal: " Whenever he responded to imperial questions he always spoke on these points, and he presented the "Six Discussions on Examining Officials," saying:
translations.idiomatic: " In audiences with the emperor he always returned to these themes, and he submitted his "Six Discussions on Examining Officials," which read:

sentences.zh: 臣謬登宰府，四年於茲，恭承德音，未嘗不以求賢為切。

translations.literal: Your subject has wrongly ascended to the chief minister's office; four years have passed, and in reverently receiving Your sagely instructions I have never failed to make seeking the worthy my urgent concern.
translations.idiomatic: I have undeservedly held a seat in the chief minister's office these four years, and in reverently receiving Your Majesty's instructions I have never ceased to make the search for talent my foremost concern.

sentences.zh: 至於延薦，職在愚臣，雖當代天之工，且乏知人之鑒；

translations.literal: As for extending recommendations, that duty rests with this foolish subject; though I perform the work of acting for Heaven, I yet lack the discernment to know men;
translations.idiomatic: As for recommending candidates, that duty falls to me; though I perform Heaven's work on Your behalf, I still lack the discernment to judge men well;

sentences.zh: 漸積歲月，負於聖明，無補王猷，有妨賢路。

translations.literal: Month by month the years have accumulated; I have failed Your sagely brilliance, added nothing to the royal plan, and obstructed the path for the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Month by month the years have piled up; I have failed Your sagely judgment, contributed nothing to the royal design, and blocked the path for worthy men.

sentences.zh: 況多疾恙，兼慮闕遺，頃奉表章，備陳肝膈。

translations.literal: Moreover I suffer many illnesses and also fear omissions and oversights; I have recently submitted a memorial fully laying bare my inmost thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I am often ill and fear I may overlook matters; I recently submitted a memorial in which I laid bare my inmost thoughts.

sentences.zh: 陛下以臣性拙直，身病可矜，不棄孱微，尚加委任。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, because my nature is blunt and upright and my illness is pitiable, did not abandon this feeble and slight person but still added to my commission.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, seeing that my nature is blunt and my illness pitiable, did not cast aside this feeble man but continued to entrust me with office.

sentences.zh: 自此思省，報效尤難，莫副堯、舜之心，空懷屍素之懼。

translations.literal: From then on, reflecting on myself, repayment of favor has become especially difficult; I cannot match the heart of Yao and Shun and can only harbor the fear of holding office in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Since then, reflecting on myself, I find it harder than ever to repay Your favor; I cannot match the intent of Yao and Shun and live only with the fear of holding office without merit.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下法象應期，聖神廣運，雲行雨施，皆發自然，訓誥典謨，悉經睿覽。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's conformity to the cosmic pattern answers the age; your sagely spirit extends far; cloudlike movement and rainlike bestowal all arise from nature; instructions, admonitions, canons, and plans have all passed through your sagely perusal.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly reflect that Your Majesty's rule accords with Heaven's season; your sagely spirit ranges far; your governance flows as naturally as clouds and rain; and every instruction and canon has passed through your wise scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 臣所以不敢援引古昔，上煩天聰，且以用人之要，願伸鄙見。

translations.literal: Therefore your subject does not dare to cite antiquity and trouble Heaven's hearing, but wishes to set forth my humble view on the essentials of employing men.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I do not dare cite antiquity and trouble Your Majesty's ear, but wish instead to offer my humble view on what matters most in the use of personnel.

sentences.zh: 復念稽顙丹陛，仰對宸嚴，謇訥易窮，遽數難辯，理詳則塵瀆頗甚，言略則利害未宣。

translations.literal: I further reflect that bowing my forehead on the cinnabar steps and looking up to answer the imperial presence—honest awkwardness is easily exhausted, and hurried enumeration is hard to argue; if the reasoning is detailed the dust of offense is rather great, if the words are brief the benefits and harms are not made clear.
translations.idiomatic: I also reflect that when I bow on the vermilion steps and answer Your Majesty face to face, my honest awkwardness is soon exhausted and hurried argument is hard to sustain: if I am too detailed I risk wearying you, yet if I am too brief the stakes are not made clear.

sentences.zh: 若默以求容，茍而竊位，縱天地之仁幸免，而中外之責何逃！

translations.literal: If I were silent to seek acceptance and held office in a perfunctory way, even if Heaven and Earth's benevolence spared me, how could I escape blame within and without!
translations.idiomatic: If I were to keep silent to win favor and hold office in a perfunctory way, even Heaven and Earth might spare me, but how could I escape blame at court and in the provinces!

sentences.zh: 非陛下用臣之意也。

translations.literal: That is not Your Majesty's intent in employing your subject.
translations.idiomatic: That is not why Your Majesty appointed me.

sentences.zh: 其所欲言者，皆陛下聖慮之內。

translations.literal: What I wish to say lies entirely within Your Majesty's sagely deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: What I wish to say lies entirely within Your Majesty's own sagely understanding.

sentences.zh: 臣以頂戴恩造，不知所為，身被風毒，漸覺沈痼，是以勤勤懇懇，切於愚誠也。

translations.literal: Your subject, bearing Your grace on my head, know not what to do; my body is afflicted by wind toxins and I gradually feel sinking chronic illness—therefore I am earnest and sincere, pressing with my foolish loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing Your grace upon my head, I scarcely know what to do; wind ailments afflict me and my illness grows chronic—hence this earnest, repeated plea born of my sincere but limited loyalty.

sentences.zh: 臣聞貞觀、開元之際，宰輔論事，或多上書，所冀獲盡情理。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that in the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan eras, when chief ministers discussed affairs they often submitted written memorials, hoping thereby to express the full reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that under the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan reigns chief ministers often submitted written memorials when discussing policy, hoping thereby to set out their reasoning fully.

sentences.zh: 今臣酌前代之損益，體當時之通變，謹獻《審官六議》，伏惟閑宴時賜省覽。

translations.literal: Now your subject has weighed the gains and losses of former ages and grasped the flexible adaptations of the present time, and respectfully presents the "Six Discussions on Examining Officials"; I humbly beg that at leisure Your Majesty grant it perusal.
translations.idiomatic: Now, weighing the strengths and weaknesses of earlier ages and the needs of our own time, I respectfully submit the "Six Discussions on Examining Officials" and humbly ask that Your Majesty read it at your leisure.

sentences.zh: 其大指，議相，則曰：「宜博采眾賢，用為輔弼。

translations.literal: Its main points: on discussing the chief minister, it says: "One should broadly gather many worthies and use them as assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Its main points are these. On the chief minister it says, "The throne should broadly gather many worthy men and employ them as assistants.

sentences.zh: 今中外知其賢者，伏願陛下用之，識其能者任之，求其全材，恐不可得。

translations.literal: Those known within and without as worthy—your subject humbly hopes Your Majesty will employ them; recognize those with ability and assign them; to seek wholly complete talent is probably unattainable.
translations.idiomatic: Those known at court and in the provinces as worthy—I humbly beg Your Majesty to employ them; recognize each man's strengths and assign him accordingly; to demand wholly perfect talent is probably impossible.

sentences.zh: 議進用庶官，則曰：「異同之論，是非難辨。

translations.literal: On discussing the promotion and use of ordinary officials, it says: "Disputes over agreement and disagreement make right and wrong hard to distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: On promoting ordinary officials it says, "When opinions clash, it is hard to tell right from wrong.

sentences.zh: 由考課難於實效，好惡雜於眾聲，所以訪之彌多，得之彌少。

translations.literal: Because performance review makes real results hard to verify and likes and dislikes are mixed in the clamor of many voices, the more one inquires the more one asks, and the less one obtains.
translations.idiomatic: Because performance reviews rarely capture real achievement and personal likes and dislikes mingle in public rumor, the more one inquires, the less one finds.

sentences.zh: 選士古今為難，拔十得五，賢愚猶半。

translations.literal: Selecting scholars has been difficult in every age; to choose ten and get five, with worthy and foolish still half and half, is already the case.
translations.idiomatic: Choosing officials has always been difficult; even to pick ten and get five worthy men, with the foolish still half the number, would be an achievement.

sentences.zh: 陛下謂臣曰：『何必五也？

translations.literal: Your Majesty said to your subject: 'Why must it be five?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty once said to me, 'Why must it be five?

sentences.zh: 十得二三斯可矣！

translations.literal: To get two or three out of ten would suffice!'
translations.idiomatic: Two or three out of ten would be enough!'

sentences.zh: 』聖主思賢至是，而宰臣不能進之，臣之罪也。

translations.literal: A sagely ruler's longing for the worthy reaches this point, yet the chief minister cannot advance them—this is your subject's crime.
translations.idiomatic: When a sage ruler longs for talent to this degree yet his chief minister cannot advance worthy men, the fault is mine.

sentences.zh: 進賢在於廣任用，明殿最，舉大節，棄其小瑕，隨其所能，試之以事，用人之大綱也。

translations.literal: Advancing the worthy lies in broad employment, clarifying rankings of merit, honoring great integrity, setting aside minor flaws, following each man's capacity, and testing him with tasks—this is the great outline of employing men.
translations.idiomatic: To advance the worthy one must employ men broadly, rank merit clearly, honor major integrity, overlook minor faults, assign each man according to his capacity, and test him in office—such is the great principle of personnel.

sentences.zh: 議京諸司闕官，則曰：「當今要官多闕，閑官十無一二。

translations.literal: On discussing vacant posts in the capital ministries, it says: "Today important offices are largely vacant, while idle offices are scarcely one or two in ten.
translations.idiomatic: On vacant posts in the capital ministries it says, "Today important offices stand largely unfilled, while superfluous posts are scarcely one or two in ten.

sentences.zh: 文武任用，資序遞遷，要官本以材行，閑官多由恩澤。

translations.literal: Civil and military appointments proceed by seniority in turn; important offices fundamentally depend on talent and conduct, while idle offices mostly come from favor and grace.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military appointments advance by seniority; important posts should go by talent and conduct, while idle posts are often filled by favor.

sentences.zh: 朝廷或將任，多擬要官則人少闕多，閑官則人多闕少；

translations.literal: When the court is about to make an appointment, if it mostly plans for important offices then people are few and vacancies many; for idle offices people are many and vacancies few;
translations.idiomatic: When the court prepares an appointment, if it favors important offices there are few candidates and many vacancies; for idle offices there are many candidates and few vacancies;

sentences.zh: 明當選拔者轉少，在優容者轉多，宜補闕員，務育材用。

translations.literal: those clearly fit for selection grow fewer, while those dwelling in indulgent ease grow more; vacant posts should be filled and nurturing talent for use should be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: those clearly fit for promotion grow fewer while those kept in comfortable sinecures grow more; vacancies should be filled and talent cultivated for service.

sentences.zh: 大廈永固，是棟梁榱桷之全也；

translations.literal: A great hall stands forever firm because beams, pillars, rafters, and brackets are all complete;
translations.idiomatic: A great hall stands firm only when beams, pillars, rafters, and brackets are all in place;

sentences.zh: 聖朝致理，亦庶官群吏之能也。

translations.literal: the sagely dynasty's attainment of good order likewise depends on the ability of the many officials and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: the sagely dynasty's good order likewise depends on the ability of its many officials and clerks.

sentences.zh: 議中外考課官，則曰：「漢以數易長吏，謂之弊政。

translations.literal: On discussing performance-review officials within and without, it says: "The Han, by frequently changing chief local officials, called it a defective policy.
translations.idiomatic: On performance-review officials at court and in the provinces it says, "The Han dynasty, by frequently rotating chief local officials, regarded that practice as a defect.

sentences.zh: 其有能理者，輒增秩賜金，或八九年、十余年，乃入為九卿，或遷三輔。

translations.literal: Those able to govern were promptly given higher rank and rewarded with gold; after eight or nine years, or more than ten, they then entered as one of the Nine Ministers or were transferred to the Three Metropolises.
translations.idiomatic: Those who governed well were promptly promoted and rewarded with gold; after eight, nine, or more than ten years they might enter the Nine Ministers or be transferred to the capital region.

sentences.zh: 功績茂異，遂至丞相，其間不隔數官。

translations.literal: With outstanding merit and achievement they might even reach chief minister, with only a few offices between.
translations.idiomatic: With outstanding achievement they might even rise to chief minister, with only a few ranks between.

sentences.zh: 今陛下內選庶僚，外委州府，課績高者，不次超升，致理之法，無逾於此。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty selects subordinate officials within and entrusts prefectures and districts without; those with high review scores are promoted out of turn—there is no better method for attaining good order.
translations.idiomatic: Today Your Majesty selects subordinates at court and entrusts the provinces without; those with outstanding reviews are promoted out of turn—no better method exists for good government.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為黜陟且立年限，若所居要重，未當遷移，就加爵秩。

translations.literal: Your subject in my foolishness think that dismissal and promotion should also set term limits; if the post held is important and transfer is not appropriate, rank and title should be added in place.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly suggest that promotions and demotions should also follow fixed terms; if a man holds an important post that should not yet change, let his rank and title be increased in place.

sentences.zh: 其余進退，令知褒貶之必應，遲速之有常。

translations.literal: For the rest, advancement and withdrawal should let men know that praise and blame will surely follow, and that delay and speed have regular patterns.
translations.idiomatic: For the rest, advancement and withdrawal should make clear that reward and censure will follow predictably, and that pace has its regular rule.

sentences.zh: 如課績在中，年考及限，與之平轉。

translations.literal: If review scores are middling and the annual examination reaches its term, give a routine transfer.
translations.idiomatic: If review scores are middling and the annual term is reached, grant a routine transfer.

sentences.zh: 中外叠處，歷試其能，使無茍且之心，又無滯淹之慮。

translations.literal: Within and without they would pass through offices in succession, testing their ability, so that there would be no perfunctory mind and no worry of stagnation and delay.
translations.idiomatic: Men would pass through offices at court and in the provinces in succession, testing their ability, so that none would grow perfunctory and none would fear being left to stagnate.

sentences.zh: 議舉遺滯，則曰：「官司既廣，必委宰輔以舉之；

translations.literal: On discussing the recommendation of overlooked and stagnant men, it says: "Since the official ranks are already broad, recommendation must be entrusted to the chief ministers;
translations.idiomatic: On recommending overlooked talent it says, "Since the bureaucracy is vast, recommendation must be entrusted to the chief ministers;

sentences.zh: 宰輔不能遍知，又詢於庶官；

translations.literal: the chief ministers cannot know everyone, so they inquire of ordinary officials;
translations.idiomatic: chief ministers cannot know everyone, so they inquire of subordinate officials;

sentences.zh: 庶官不能遍知，又訪於眾人。

translations.literal: ordinary officials cannot know everyone, so they inquire of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: subordinates cannot know everyone, so they inquire of the public at large.

sentences.zh: 眾聲囂然，互有臧否，十人舉之未信，一人毀之可疑，迨至於今，茲弊未改。

translations.literal: The clamor of many voices rises, each side praising or condemning; ten men recommend and it is not yet believed, one man slanders and doubt arises—down to today this abuse has not changed.
translations.idiomatic: Voices clamor on every side with praise and blame; ten men may recommend someone and he is still doubted, one man may slander him and he becomes suspect—down to today this abuse remains.

sentences.zh: 其所以然者，非盡為愛憎也，苦於不審實而承聲言之。

translations.literal: The reason is not entirely personal love and hate; the hardship lies in not verifying facts and repeating what one has merely heard.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is not wholly personal favor or spite; the trouble is that men repeat hearsay without verifying facts.

sentences.zh: 大凡常人之心，以稱人之善為清，以攻人之過為直，茍有除授，多生橫議。

translations.literal: Generally the mind of ordinary people takes praising another's goodness as purity and attacking another's faults as uprightness; whenever there is an appointment or grant, many reckless disputes arise.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary men commonly treat praise as disinterested purity and attack as blunt honesty; whenever an appointment is made, reckless disputes multiply.

sentences.zh: 由是宰臣每將薦用，亦自重難，日往月來，未副聖意。

translations.literal: Because of this, whenever chief ministers were about to recommend someone for use they also grew heavily cautious; day followed month and still they failed to match the sagely intent.
translations.idiomatic: Hence whenever chief ministers were about to recommend someone they grew excessively cautious; days and months passed without satisfying Your Majesty's intent.

sentences.zh: 宜須采聽時論，以所舉多者先用，必非大故，皆不棄之。

translations.literal: One should gather and heed contemporary opinion, using first those most often recommended; unless the fault is grave, none should be cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: The court should heed contemporary opinion and employ first those most often recommended; unless the fault is grave, none should be discarded.

sentences.zh: 議擢用諸使府僚屬，則曰：「諸使辟吏，各自精求，務於得人，將重府望。

translations.literal: On discussing the promotion of staff from the various commissioner offices, it says: "The commissioners' recruited clerks each seek men with care, striving to obtain talent and thereby enhance the prestige of their offices.
translations.idiomatic: On promoting staff from commissioner offices it says, "Each commissioner recruits his staff with care, striving to obtain talent and thereby enhance his office's standing.

sentences.zh: 既經試效，能否可知，擢其賢能，置之朝列。

translations.literal: Once they have been tested in performance, ability or inability can be known; promote the worthy and able and place them in the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Once they have been tested in office, their ability is known; promote the worthy among them and place them in the court ranks.

sentences.zh: 或曰外使須才，固不可奪。

translations.literal: Some say the outer commissioners need talent and therefore must not be deprived of it.
translations.idiomatic: Some say frontier commissioners need talent and therefore cannot be deprived of it.

sentences.zh: 臣知必不然也。

translations.literal: Your subject knows this is certainly not so.
translations.idiomatic: I know that cannot be so.

sentences.zh: 屬者使府賓介，每有登朝，本使殊以為榮，自喜知人，且明公選。

translations.literal: Recently, whenever staff from commissioner offices entered court service, their original commissioner took it as special honor, pleased with himself for knowing men and showing that public selection was clear.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, whenever a commissioner's staff member entered court service, his commissioner took it as a special honor, pleased that he had recognized talent and that public selection was sound.

sentences.zh: 大凡才能之士，名位未達，多在方鎮。

translations.literal: Generally men of ability whose fame and rank have not yet risen are mostly in the regional commands.
translations.idiomatic: Generally, men of ability whose names and ranks have not yet risen are found chiefly in the regional commands.

sentences.zh: 日月在上，誰不知之，思登闕庭，如望霄漢，宜須博采，無宜久滯。

translations.literal: The sun and moon are above—who does not know it? They long to ascend the court of the palace gate as if gazing toward the Milky Way; they should be broadly gathered and ought not long to stagnate.
translations.idiomatic: The throne shines above—who does not see it? They long to enter the palace court as if gazing toward the heavens; they should be broadly recruited and not left to stagnate.

sentences.zh: 」上優詔答之。

translations.literal: " The emperor answered with an excellent edict.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied with a gracious edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 時吏部侍郎杜黃裳為中貴讒譖及他過犯，御史中丞穆贊、京兆少尹韋武、萬年縣令李宣、長安令盧雲，皆為裴延齡構陷，將加斥逐。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Minister of Personnel Du Huangchang was slandered by inner eunuchs and implicated in other offenses; Vice Censor-in-Chief Mu Zan, Junior Assistant Metropolitan Governor Wei Wu, Magistrate of Wannian Li Xuan, and Magistrate of Chang'an Lu Yun were all framed by Pei Yanling and were about to be expelled and driven off.
translations.idiomatic: At that time vice minister of personnel Du Huangchang was slandered by palace eunuchs and charged with other offenses; vice censor-in-chief Mu Zan, junior metropolitan assistant governor Wei Wu, magistrate of Wannian Li Xuan, and magistrate of Chang'an Lu Yun had all been framed by Pei Yanling and were about to be expelled.

sentences.zh: 憬保護救解之，故多從輕貶。

translations.literal: Jing protected and rescued them, so most received only light demotions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jing protected and secured their release, so most received only light demotions.

sentences.zh: 初，憬廉察湖南，令狐峘、崔儆並為巡屬刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jing inspected Hunan, Linghu Dan and Cui Yi both served as touring subordinate prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Jing served as Hunan inspection commissioner, Linghu Dan and Cui Yi both served as touring subordinate prefects under him.

sentences.zh: 峘嘗歷中書舍人、禮部侍郎，儆久在朝列，所為或虧法令，憬每以正道制之。

translations.literal: Dan had formerly served as Secretariat Drafter and Vice Minister of Rites; Yi had long been in the court ranks; their conduct sometimes fell short of law and regulation, and Jing each time restrained them by the correct path.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Dan had formerly served as secretariat drafter and vice minister of rites; Cui Yi had long served at court; their conduct sometimes violated the law, and Zhao Jing repeatedly restrained them on proper grounds.

sentences.zh: 峘、儆密遣人數憬罪狀，毀之於朝。

translations.literal: Dan and Yi secretly sent men repeatedly to enumerate Jing's offenses and slandered him at court.
translations.idiomatic: Dan and Yi secretly sent men to enumerate Zhao Jing's offenses again and again and slandered him at court.

sentences.zh: 及憬為相，拔儆自大理卿為尚書右丞，峘先貶官為別駕，又擢為吉州刺史，時人多之。

translations.literal: When Jing became chief minister he promoted Yi from Director of the Court of Judicial Review to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Dan, who had first been demoted to assistant prefect, was also raised to Prefect of Jizhou, and people of the time mostly praised this.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Jing became chief minister he promoted Cui Yi from director of the Court of Judicial Review to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs; Linghu Dan, though earlier demoted to assistant prefect, was also raised to prefect of Jizhou, and contemporaries widely praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 憬與陸贄同知政事。

translations.literal: Jing and Lu Zhi jointly directed state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jing and Lu Zhi jointly directed state affairs.

sentences.zh: 贄恃久在禁庭，特承恩顧，以國政為己任，才周歲，轉憬為門下侍郎。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi relied on his long service in the inner palace and special imperial favor, took national affairs as his own responsibility, and after only a full year transferred Jing to Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, relying on his long service in the inner palace and special imperial favor, took national affairs as his own charge; after only a year he transferred Zhao Jing to vice director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 憬由是深銜之，數以目疾請告，不甚當政事，因是不相協。

translations.literal: Jing therefore deeply resented him, repeatedly requested leave on grounds of eye illness, and did not much attend to state affairs; because of this they were not in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jing therefore deeply resented him, repeatedly requested leave on grounds of eye trouble, and attended little to state affairs; the two were thus not in harmony.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡奸詐恣睢，滿朝側目。

translations.literal: Pei Yanling was treacherous, deceitful, and overbearing; the whole court looked askance at him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling was treacherous, deceitful, and overbearing; the whole court looked on him with distaste.

sentences.zh: 憬初與贄約於上前論之，及延英奏對，贄極言延齡奸邪誑誕之狀，不可任用。

translations.literal: Jing had at first agreed with Lu Zhi to discuss this before the throne; when they presented at the Yanying audience, Lu Zhi spoke at length of Yanling's treacherous, depraved, and deceitful conduct and that he could not be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jing had at first agreed with Lu Zhi to raise the matter before the throne; at the Yanying audience Lu Zhi spoke at length of Yanling's treachery and deceit and argued that he must not be employed.

sentences.zh: 德宗不悅，形於顏色。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong was displeased, and it showed in his countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong was displeased, and it showed plainly on his face.

sentences.zh: 憬默然無言，由是罷贄平章事，而憬當國矣。

translations.literal: Jing remained silent without a word; because of this Lu Zhi was removed from the grand councilorship, and Jing then directed the state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jing remained silent; Lu Zhi was thereupon removed from the grand councilorship, and Zhao Jing then directed the state.

sentences.zh: 時宰相賈耽、盧邁與憬三人。

translations.literal: At that time the chief ministers were Jia Dan, Lu Mai, and Jing—three in all.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the chief ministers were Jia Dan, Lu Mai, and Zhao Jing—three in all.

sentences.zh: 十二年春正月，耽、邁皆有假，故憬獨對於延英。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, spring, first month, Dan and Mai both had leave, so Jing alone answered at Yanying.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the twelfth year, Jia Dan and Lu Mai were both on leave, so Zhao Jing alone attended audience in the Yanying Hall.

sentences.zh: 上問曰：「近日起居註記何事？

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "What have the Records of Attendance and Note recently recorded?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "What have the daily recorders been noting in recent days?

sentences.zh: 」憬對曰：「古者左史記言，人君動止，有實言隨即記錄，起居註是也。

translations.literal: Jing replied: "In antiquity the left scribe recorded speech; the ruler's movements and stops—whenever there were actual words, they were immediately recorded; this is the Records of Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jing replied: "In antiquity the left scribe recorded the ruler's words—whenever the sovereign spoke in earnest, it was written down at once. That is what the Records of Daily Life and Activities are.

sentences.zh: 國朝永徽中，起居唯得對仗承旨，仗下後謀議皆不得聞，其記註唯編制敕，更無他事。

translations.literal: In our dynasty during the Yonghui era, attendance officials only received imperial intent while standing in formation at court; after dismissal from formation, deliberations could not be heard; their records only compiled edicts, with nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty, during the Yonghui reign, recorders only received the emperor's directives while standing in formation at court audiences. After the formation was dismissed, they could hear none of the deliberations, and their notes amounted merely to compiling edicts—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 所以長壽中姚璹知政事，以為親承德音謨訓，若不宣旨，宰相、史官無以得書。

translations.literal: Therefore during the Changshou era Yao Qi controlled state affairs; he considered that to personally receive the virtuous sound and instructive words, if the intent were not proclaimed, chief ministers and historiographers would have no way to record.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason, during the Changshou era, when Yao Qi served in the chief council, he argued that because ministers personally received the emperor's words and instructions, if those directives were not formally announced, neither the chief ministers nor the historiographers would have anything to record.

sentences.zh: 璹請宰相一人記錄所論軍國政事，謂之時政記，每月送史館。

translations.literal: Qi requested that one chief minister record discussions of military and state affairs, calling it the Record of Current Affairs, sent monthly to the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Qi proposed that one chief minister keep a record of deliberations on military and state affairs—a work called the Record of Current Affairs—to be sent each month to the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 既而時政記又廢。

translations.literal: Subsequently the Record of Current Affairs was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In time, the Record of Current Affairs was abolished once more.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「君舉必書，義存勸誡。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The ruler's actions must be written; the principle lies in encouragement and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "A ruler's conduct must be committed to writing—the point is to preserve encouragement and admonition.

sentences.zh: 既嘗有時政記，宰臣宜依故事為之。

translations.literal: Since there once was a Record of Current Affairs, chief ministers should follow precedent in doing this.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Record of Current Affairs existed before, the chief ministers should reinstate it according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 」無何，憬卒，時政記亦不行。

translations.literal: Before long, Jing died, and the Record of Current Affairs was also not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhao Jing died, and the Record of Current Affairs was never implemented.

sentences.zh: 憬特承恩顧，性清儉，雖為宰輔，居第仆使，類貧士大夫之家，所得俸入，先置私廟，而竟不立第舍田產。

translations.literal: Jing especially received imperial favor; his nature was pure and frugal; although he was a chief minister, his residence's servants resembled those of impoverished scholar-official households; the salary he received was first used to establish a private ancestral shrine, yet in the end he never established a residence or farmland.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jing enjoyed exceptional imperial favor, yet his character was austere and frugal. Though he served as a chief minister, the servants at his home were like those of a poor scholar-official's household. He devoted his salary first to maintaining a private ancestral shrine and never acquired a lavish residence or landed estate.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，遇暴疾，信宿而卒，時年六十一。

translations.literal: That year in the eighth month, he encountered a sudden illness; after one night he died; at the time he was sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of that year he was stricken with a sudden illness and died within two days. He was sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 子元亮進憬遺表草曰：「臣叨荷聖慈，竊塵臺鼎，年序頗久，績用無聞，負乘之敗已彰，覆餗之咎俄及。

translations.literal: His son Yuanliang presented Jing's draft memorial: "Your subject undeservedly bears holy grace, secretly occupying the summit of the tripod; years have been quite long, achievements have not been heard of; the failure of an overloaded carriage is already manifest, the fault of overturned soup suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao Yuanliang submitted Zhao Jing's draft memorial, which read: "Your humble servant has undeservedly received Your Majesty's grace and occupied a seat at the highest council. Years have passed, yet I have accomplished nothing of note. The disaster of an overloaded carriage is already plain upon me, and the calamity of overturned soup has suddenly befallen.

sentences.zh: 而天與之疾，福過生災，自今日卯時以來，稍加困重，針灸不及，藥餌奚施。

translations.literal: Heaven gave him illness; excess fortune gave birth to disaster; from the mao hour today onward, gradually more distressed and grave; acupuncture unable to reach, what use medicine?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has afflicted me with illness—fortune run too high has bred calamity. Since the mao hour this morning my condition has steadily worsened. Acupuncture could not help; medicines availed nothing.

sentences.zh: 奄然遊魂，終當就木，冥冥殘喘，豈忍辭天！

translations.literal: Suddenly a wandering soul, ultimately must go to wood; in dimness lingering breath, how can bear to leave Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: My soul is already departing; soon I must go to my coffin. With only faint breaths left in the darkness, how can I bear to leave Your Majesty's grace!

sentences.zh: 號呼涕零，側息心斷，反風結草，誓報深恩，雖死猶生，豈孤素願。

translations.literal: Crying out tears falling, side breath heart broken, reverse wind tied grass, sworn to repay deep grace, though dead still alive, how abandon lifelong wish.
translations.idiomatic: I cry out and weep; my heart breaks with every labored breath. Like the grasses that bowed before the wind and Zhong Kui's spirit that tied stalks in gratitude, I swear to repay your profound kindness—even in death I live on—how could I betray my lifelong devotion?

sentences.zh: 無任感恩，嗚咽痛恨之至。

translations.literal: Unable to bear gratitude, sobbing and bitter regret to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot contain my gratitude; this is my deepest sobbing grief and remorse.

sentences.zh: 」德宗尤悼惜之，廢朝三日，冊贈太子太傅，賻帛五百端、米粟四百石，令鴻臚卿王權充冊吊使。

translations.literal: Dezong especially mourned and treasured him; cancelled court three days; by edict posthumously appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; condolence gifts of five hundred bolts of silk and four hundred shi of grain and rice; ordered Minister of Ceremonies Wang Quan to serve as enfeoffment and condolence envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong deeply mourned him. Court was suspended for three days. Zhao Jing was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, with five hundred bolts of silk and four hundred shi of grain and rice as condolence gifts. Wang Quan, Minister of Ceremonies, was appointed envoy to convey the enfeoffment and condolences.

sentences.zh: 元亮官至左司郎中、侍御史知雜事卒。

translations.literal: Yuanliang reached office of Left Department Director, Palace Censor supervising miscellaneous affairs, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yuanliang rose to Left Department Director and Palace Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs before his death.

sentences.zh: 次子全亮，官至侍御史、桂管防禦判官。

translations.literal: Second son Quanliang, reached office of Palace Censor, Guiguan Defense adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: The second son, Zhao Quanliang, served as Palace Censor and adjutant for the Guiguan Defense command.

sentences.zh: 元亮兄宣亮、弟承亮，皆以門廕授官。

translations.literal: Yuanliang's elder brother Xuanliang and younger brother Chengliang both received offices through yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang's elder brother Xuanliang and younger brother Chengliang both received their posts through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 韋倫韋倫，開元、天寶中朔方節度使光乘之子。

translations.literal: Wei Lun, Wei Lun, son of Guangcheng, Shuofang military commissioner during Kaiyuan and Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lun was the son of Wei Guangcheng, military commissioner of Shuofang during the Kaiyuan and Tianbao reigns.

sentences.zh: 少以廕累授藍田縣尉。

translations.literal: In youth through yin succession appointed Lantian county lieutenant.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he received appointment as magistrate's aide of Lantian County through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 以吏事勤恪，楊國忠署為鑄錢內作使判官。

translations.literal: Because of diligent and conscientious clerical affairs, Yang Guozhong appointed him assistant magistrate of the Minting Inner Works Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Recognized for diligence in administrative work, he was appointed by Yang Guozhong as adjutant to the Commissioner of the Minting Inner Works.

sentences.zh: 國忠恃權寵，又邀名稱，多征諸州縣農人令鑄錢。

translations.literal: Guozhong relied on power and favor, and also sought reputation; frequently conscripted farmers from various prefectures and counties to make coin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong abused his power and court favor and sought popular acclaim. He conscripted farmers from prefectures and counties across the empire to mint coins.

sentences.zh: 農夫既非本色工匠，被所由抑令就役，多遭箠罰，人不聊生。

translations.literal: Farmers were not proper artisan craftsmen; coerced by local authorities to take service, many suffered beating punishment; people could not sustain life.
translations.idiomatic: These farmers were not trained craftsmen. Local officials forced them into service, and many were beaten with rods. The people could scarcely survive.

sentences.zh: 倫白國忠曰：「鑄錢須得本色人，今抑百姓農人為之，尤費力無功，人且興謗。

translations.literal: Lun told Guozhong: "Coin minting must obtain proper personnel; now coercing common people and farmers to do it, especially wastes strength without success; people will raise slander.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lun told Yang Guozhong: "Minting requires skilled workers. Pressing peasants and farmers into the task wastes labor for little result and will provoke public resentment.

sentences.zh: 請厚懸市估價，募工曉者為之。

translations.literal: Request to generously post market appraisal prices, recruit skilled knowing workers to do it.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that you post generous market wages and recruit workers who know the craft.

sentences.zh: 」由是役使減少，而益鑄錢之數。

translations.literal: From this corvée labor decreased, yet increased the amount of minted coin.
translations.idiomatic: As a result forced labor declined while the volume of coin minted actually increased.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，宮內土木之功無虛日，內作人吏因緣為奸，倫乃躬親閱視，省費減倍。

translations.literal: At end of Tianbao, palace civil engineering work had no idle day; inner works clerks took opportunity to commit wrongdoing; Lun then personally inspected, saving expense reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Tianbao era, palace construction went on every day without pause. Inner-works officials exploited the opportunity for corruption. Wei Lun personally inspected the work and cut costs by half.

sentences.zh: 改大理評事。

translations.literal: Changed to Dali court reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of court reviewer in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 會安祿山反，車駕幸蜀，拜倫監察御史、劍南節度行軍司馬，兼充置頓使判官，尋改屯田員外、兼侍御史。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, imperial carriage went to Shu; appointed Lun as investigating censor, Jiannan circuit expeditionary army vice marshal, also serving as encampment commissioner adjutant; soon changed to Field Commissioner outside director, concurrently Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled and the emperor fled to Shu, Wei Lun was appointed investigating censor and vice marshal of the Jiannan expeditionary army, with additional duty as adjutant to the encampment commissioner. He was soon promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue and concurrent Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 時內官禁軍相次到蜀，所在侵暴，號為難理；

translations.literal: At that time eunuchs and imperial guards arrived in succession at Shu; wherever they were, they invaded and plundered, called difficult to govern;
translations.idiomatic: At that time palace eunuchs and imperial guards arrived in Shu one after another. Wherever they went they plundered, and the region was said to be nearly ungovernable.

sentences.zh: 倫清儉，率身以化之，蜀川鹹賴其理。

translations.literal: Lun was pure and frugal; led himself to reform them; all of Sichuan relied on his governance.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lun was upright and frugal and led by personal example. All of Sichuan benefited from his administration.

sentences.zh: 竟遭中官毀譖，貶衡州司戶。

translations.literal: Ultimately suffered eunuchs' slanderous accusations, demoted to Hengzhou revenue clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was slandered by eunuchs and demoted to revenue clerk of Heng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 屬東都、河南並陷賊，漕運路絕，度支使第五琦薦倫有理能，拜商州刺史，充荊襄等道租庸使。

translations.literal: As Eastern Capital and Henan both fell to rebels, transport routes cut off, Fiscal Commissioner Diwu Qi recommended Lun had governing ability, appointed Shangzhou prefect, served as Jing-Xiang circuit rent and corvée commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When both the Eastern Capital and Henan fell to the rebels and grain transport routes were severed, Fiscal Commissioner Diwu Qi recommended Wei Lun for his administrative talent. He was appointed prefect of Shang Prefecture and commissioner for rent and corvée on the Jing-Xiang route.

sentences.zh: 會襄州裨將康楚元、張嘉延聚眾為叛，兇黨萬余人，自稱東楚義王。

translations.literal: When Xiangzhou lieutenant generals Kang Chuyuan and Zhang Jiayan gathered crowds to rebel, fierce faction over ten thousand, proclaimed themselves Eastern Chu Righteous King.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiangzhou lieutenant generals Kang Chuyuan and Zhang Jiayan raised a rebellion with more than ten thousand followers, proclaiming themselves kings of Eastern Chu.

sentences.zh: 襄州刺史王政棄城遁走。

translations.literal: Xiangzhou prefect Wang Zheng abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zheng, prefect of Xiang Prefecture, abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 嘉延又南襲破江陵，漢、沔饋運阻絕，朝廷旰食。

translations.literal: Jiayan again south attacked and captured Jiangling; Han and Mian supply transport obstructed and cut off; court ate late meals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiayan then marched south and seized Jiangling, blocking supply lines along the Han and Mian rivers. The court went without proper meals for worry.

sentences.zh: 倫乃調發兵甲駐鄧州界，兇黨有來降者，必厚加接待。

translations.literal: Lun then mobilized troops stationed at Dengzhou border; of the fierce faction those who came to surrender, certainly treated hospitably.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lun gathered troops and encamped them on the border of Deng Prefecture. Anyone who came over from the rebels was received with generous hospitality.

sentences.zh: 數日後，楚元眾頗怠，倫進軍擊之。

translations.literal: After several days, Chuyuan's crowd grew somewhat slack; Lun advanced army and struck them.
translations.idiomatic: After several days Kang Chuyuan's forces grew lax, and Wei Lun marched against them.

sentences.zh: 生擒楚元以獻，余眾悉走散，收租庸錢物僅二百萬貫，並不失墜。

translations.literal: Captured Chuyuan alive and presented; remaining crowd all scattered and fled; collected rent and corvée money and goods nearly two million strings, all without loss.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Kang Chuyuan alive and sent him to the capital. The rest of the rebels dispersed. He recovered nearly two million strings' worth of rent and corvée goods without losing a single item.

sentences.zh: 荊、襄二州平。

translations.literal: Jing and Xiang two prefectures pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing and Xiang regions were pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔除崔光遠為襄州節度使，征倫為衛尉卿。

translations.literal: Edict appointing Cui Guangyuan as Xiangzhou military commissioner, summoning Lun as Minister of Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Cui Guangyuan military commissioner of Xiang Prefecture and recalled Wei Lun to serve as Minister of Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 旬日，又以本官兼寧州刺史、招討處置等使，尋又兼隴州刺史。

translations.literal: Within ten days, again with original office concurrently Ningzhou prefect, pacification and disposal commissioner etc.; soon also concurrently Longzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he was also made prefect of Ning Prefecture and commissioner for pacification and disposal, and soon after concurrently prefect of Long Prefecture while retaining his original rank.

sentences.zh: 乾元三年，襄州大將張瑾殺節度使史翙作亂，乃以倫為襄州刺史、兼御史大夫、山南東道襄鄧等十州節度使。

translations.literal: Qianyuan third year, Xiangzhou great general Zhang Jin killed military commissioner Shi Hui and rebelled; then appointed Lun as Xiangzhou prefect, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Shannan East Circuit Xiang-Deng ten prefecture military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianyuan, the Xiangzhou general Zhang Jin killed the military commissioner Shi Hui and rebelled. Wei Lun was appointed prefect of Xiang Prefecture, Censor-in-Chief, and military commissioner over ten prefectures of the Shannan East Circuit including Xiang and Deng.

sentences.zh: 時李輔國秉權用事，節將除拜，皆出其門。

translations.literal: At that time Li Fuguo wielded power; military commissioners' appointments and dismissals all came from his gate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Fuguo held power, and appointments of regional commanders all passed through his faction.

sentences.zh: 倫既為朝廷公用，又不私謁輔國。

translations.literal: Lun was both used publicly by the court, yet did not privately visit Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lun had been appointed on merit for the state's service and did not pay private calls on Li Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 倫受命未行，改秦州刺史、兼御史中丞、本州防禦使。

translations.literal: Lun received appointment but had not departed; changed to Qinzhou prefect, concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, that prefecture defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wei Lun could take up his new post, he was reassigned as prefect of Qin Prefecture, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and defense commissioner of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃、党項歲歲入寇，邊將奔命不暇。

translations.literal: At that time Tibetans and Tangut tribes yearly invaded; border generals had no leisure for anything but rushing to duty.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetans and Tangut tribes raided the borders year after year, and frontier commanders had scarcely a moment's rest.

sentences.zh: 倫至秦州，屢與虜戰。

translations.literal: Lun reached Qinzhou, repeatedly fought with barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Lun arrived at Qin Prefecture, he fought the invaders repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 兵寡無援，頻致敗衄，連貶巴州長史、思州務川縣尉。

translations.literal: Troops few without reinforcement, frequently brought defeat; in succession demoted to Bazhou chief secretary, Sizhou Wuchuan county magistrate aide.
translations.idiomatic: With too few troops and no reinforcements, he suffered repeated defeats and was demoted in succession to chief secretary of Ba Prefecture and then magistrate's aide of Wuchuan County in Si Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，起為忠州刺史，歷臺、饒二州。

translations.literal: Daizong took throne, raised as Zhongzhou prefect, passed through Tai and Rao two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong ascended the throne, Wei Lun was recalled and served as prefect of Zhong Prefecture, then of Tai and Rao Prefectures in turn.

sentences.zh: 以中官呂太一於嶺南矯詔募兵為亂，乃以倫為韶州刺史、兼御史中丞、韶連柳三州都團練使。

translations.literal: Because eunuch Lü Taiyi in Lingnan forged edict to raise troops and rebel, then appointed Lun as Shaozhou prefect, concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, Shao-Lian-Liu three prefectures unified training commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Lü Taiyi forged an imperial edict in Lingnan to raise troops in revolt, Wei Lun was appointed prefect of Shao Prefecture, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and unified training commissioner over Shao, Lian, and Liu Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 竟遭太一用賂反間，貶信州司馬、虔州司戶、隋州司戶、隨州司馬。

translations.literal: Ultimately suffered Taiyi using bribes and counter-intelligence; demoted to Xinzhou vice prefect, Qianzhou revenue clerk, Suizhou revenue clerk, Suizhou vice prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Lü Taiyi used bribery and counter-intelligence against him. Wei Lun was demoted in succession to vice prefect of Xin Prefecture, revenue clerk of Qian Prefecture, revenue clerk of Sui Prefecture, and vice prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 遇赦，旅寓於洪州十數年。

translations.literal: Met amnesty, sojourned lodged at Hongzhou over ten years.
translations.idiomatic: After a general amnesty he lived as an exile in Hong Prefecture for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，選堪使絕域者，征倫拜太常少卿、兼御史中丞，持節充通和吐蕃使。

translations.literal: Dezong took throne; selected those able to serve distant regions; summoned Lun appointed Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, bearing staff as envoy to communicate peace with Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong ascended the throne, he sought men capable of missions to distant lands. Wei Lun was summoned, appointed Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and Vice Censor-in-Chief, and sent as envoy to negotiate peace with Tibet.

sentences.zh: 倫至蕃中，初宣諭皇恩，次述國威德遠振，蕃人大悅，贊普入獻方物。

translations.literal: Lun reached among Tibetans; first proclaimed imperial grace, next described state's power and virtue far-reaching; Tibetan people greatly pleased; zanpu came to offer local products.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Lun reached Tibet, he first conveyed the emperor's benevolence and then described the empire's far-reaching might and virtue. The Tibetans were delighted, and the zanpu came to offer tribute.

sentences.zh: 使還，遷太常卿、兼御史大夫，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Mission returned; promoted to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrent Censor-in-Chief; added Silver Light Chamberlain Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and Censor-in-Chief, with the honorary rank of Silver Light Chamberlain Grandee.

sentences.zh: 再入吐蕃，奉使稱旨，西蕃敬服。

translations.literal: Again entered Tibet; mission accorded with intent; Western Tibetans respectfully submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On a second mission to Tibet his embassy fully satisfied the court, and the western Tibetans held him in respect.

sentences.zh: 朝廷得失，數上疏言之。

translations.literal: Court's gains and losses, repeatedly submitted memorials to speak of them.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted memorials on the court's strengths and failings.

sentences.zh: 又為宰相盧杞所惡，改太子少保，累加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Also was hated by chief minister Lu Qi; changed to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; cumulatively added Grand General of the Household with Full Ceremonial Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He also earned the hatred of the chief minister Lu Qi and was transferred to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, though he was eventually granted the honorary title of Grand General of the Household with Full Ceremonial Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 涇師之亂，駕幸奉天。

translations.literal: Jing military rebellion; carriage visited Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: During the rebellion of the Jingzhou garrison, the emperor fled to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 及盧杞、白誌貞、趙贊等貶官，關播罷相為刑部尚書，倫於朝堂嗚咽而言曰：「宰相不能弼諧啟沃，使天下一至於此。

translations.literal: When Lu Qi, Bai Zhen, Zhao Zan and others demoted; Guan Bo removed from chancellorship to Minister of Justice; Lun at court hall sobbed and spoke: "Chief ministers could not assist and harmonize, open and nurture; caused all under Heaven to reach this point.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Qi, Bai Zhen, Zhao Zan, and others were demoted and Guan Bo was dismissed from the chancellorship to become Minister of Justice, Wei Lun sobbed aloud in the hall of audience and said: "The chief ministers failed to counsel and harmonize the throne, and brought the empire to this pass.

sentences.zh: 仍為尚書，天下何由致理？

translations.literal: Still serving as Minister; how can all under Heaven achieve good governance?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guan Bo remains a minister—how is the empire ever to be well governed?

sentences.zh: 」聞者敬憚之。

translations.literal: Hearers respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard him respected and feared him in equal measure.

sentences.zh: 從駕梁州，還京，又欲擢用盧杞為饒州刺史。

translations.literal: Following carriage to Liangzhou, returning capital; again wanted to promote Lu Qi as Raozhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: After following the emperor to Liangzhou and returning to the capital, the court again sought to appoint Lu Qi prefect of Rao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 倫又上表切言不可，深為忠正之士所稱嘆。

translations.literal: Lun again submitted memorial sharply saying not permissible; deeply praised by loyal upright gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lun again submitted a forceful memorial declaring the appointment unacceptable, winning deep acclaim from upright officials.

sentences.zh: 以年逾七十，表請休官，改太子少師致仕，封郢國公。

translations.literal: Because age exceeded seventy, submitted memorial requesting retirement from office; changed to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent retired; enfeoffed as Duke of Ying state.
translations.idiomatic: When he passed seventy he requested retirement and was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent emeritus, enfeoffed as Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 時李楚琳以僕射兼衛尉卿，李忠誠以尚書兼少府監，倫上言曰：「楚琳兇逆，忠誠蕃戎醜類，不合廁列清班。

translations.literal: At that time Li Chulin as Vice Director concurrently Minister of Imperial Guards, Li Zhongcheng as Minister concurrently Director of the Palace Storehouses; Lun submitted saying: "Chulin is fierce and rebellious, Zhongcheng is ugly barbarian type, not fitting to stand in pure ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Chulin served as Vice Director and Minister of Imperial Guards, and Li Zhongcheng as Minister and Director of the Palace Storehouses. Wei Lun submitted a memorial: "Li Chulin is treacherous and rebellious; Li Zhongcheng is a disgraceful foreign mercenary. Neither belongs in the court's highest ranks.

sentences.zh: 」又表請置義倉以防水旱，擇賢良任之左右。

translations.literal: Also memorial requested establishing charity granaries to guard against flood and drought, select worthy and good to serve at left and right.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to establish charity granaries against flood and drought and to select worthy men to serve close to the throne.

sentences.zh: 又言吐蕃必無信約，專須防備，不可輕易。

translations.literal: Also said Tibet certainly has no trustworthy agreement, must specially need defense preparation, cannot be lightly [trusted].
translations.idiomatic: He further warned that Tibet would never keep its agreements and must be guarded against—not treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 上每善遇之。

translations.literal: Emperor always treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor always received him graciously.

sentences.zh: 倫居家孝友，撫弟侄以慈愛稱。

translations.literal: Lun at home was filial and friendly; raised younger brothers and nephews, famed for kindness and love.
translations.idiomatic: At home Wei Lun was filial and devoted to his kin; he was renowned for the loving care he showed his brothers and nephews.

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年十二月卒，時年八十三，贈揚州都督。

translations.literal: Zhenyuan fourteenth year twelfth month died; at the time age eighty-three; posthumously granted Yangzhou area commander.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan at the age of eighty-three and was posthumously granted the title of Area Commander of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 賈耽賈耽，字敦詩，滄州南皮人。

translations.literal: Jia Dan, Jia Dan, style name Dunshi, native of Nanpi, Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dan, styled Dunshi, was a native of Nanpi in Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以兩經登第，調授貝州臨清縣尉。

translations.literal: Through two classics passed examination; transferred appointed Beizhou Linqing county lieutenant.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in both Classics and was appointed magistrate's aide of Linqing County in Bei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上疏論時政，授絳州正平尉。

translations.literal: Submitted memorial discussing current affairs; appointed Jiangzhou Zhengping county lieutenant.
translations.idiomatic: After submitting a memorial on current affairs, he was appointed magistrate's aide of Zhengping County in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從事河東，檢校膳部員外郎、太原少尹、北都副留守。

translations.literal: Served in Hedong; provisional Food Department outside director, Taiyuan Vice Governor, Northern Capital Deputy Protector.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Hedong as provisional vice director in the Ministry of Rites, Vice Governor of Taiyuan, and Deputy Protector of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 又檢校禮部郎中、節度副使，改汾州刺史。

translations.literal: Also provisional Rites Department director, military commissioner vice commissioner; changed to Fenzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made provisional director in the Ministry of Rites and vice commissioner of the circuit, then transferred to prefect of Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在郡七年，政績茂異。

translations.literal: At the prefecture seven years; governance achievements lush and exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: He governed the prefecture for seven years with outstanding achievements.

sentences.zh: 入為鴻臚卿，時左右威遠營隸鴻臚，耽仍領其使。

translations.literal: Entered court as Minister of Ceremonies; at that time Left and Right Weiyuan camps subordinate to Ceremonies; Dan still led that commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Minister of Ceremonies. The Left and Right Weiyuan camps were then under that ministry, and Jia Dan continued to direct them.

sentences.zh: 大歷十四年十一月，檢校左散騎常侍、兼梁州刺史、御史大夫、山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: Dali fourteenth year eleventh month; provisional Left Regular Attendant; concurrently Liangzhou prefect, Censor-in-Chief, Shannan West Circuit military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourteenth year of Dali he was made provisional Left Regular Attendant, prefect of Liang Prefecture, Censor-in-Chief, and military commissioner of the Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 建中三年十一月，檢校工部尚書、兼御史大夫、山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: Jianzhong third year eleventh month; provisional Minister of Works, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Shannan East Circuit military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year of Jianzhong he was made provisional Minister of Works, Censor-in-Chief, and military commissioner of the Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 德宗移幸梁州。

translations.literal: Dezong moved fortune to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong moved the court to Liang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 興元元年二月，耽使行軍司馬樊澤奏事於行在，澤既復命，方大宴諸將，有急牒至，言澤代耽為節度使，而召耽為工部尚書。

translations.literal: Xingyuan first year second month; Dan sent expeditionary army vice marshal Fan Ze to report at the traveling palace; Ze had returned report, just then greatly feasting the generals; urgent dispatch arrived saying Ze replaced Dan as military commissioner, and summoned Dan as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Xingyuan, Jia Dan sent his expeditionary vice marshal Fan Ze to report to the imperial camp. After Fan Ze returned and a grand banquet for the generals was underway, an urgent dispatch arrived announcing that Fan Ze would replace Jia Dan as military commissioner and that Jia Dan was summoned to serve as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 耽得牒內懷中，宴飲不改容。

translations.literal: Dan received dispatch inside bosom; banquet drinking did not change expression.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dan slipped the dispatch inside his robe and showed no change of expression during the feast.

sentences.zh: 及散，召樊澤，以詔授之曰：「詔以行軍為節度使，耽今即上路。

translations.literal: When dispersed; summoned Fan Ze; with edict conferred it saying: "Edict appoints expeditionary army as military commissioner; Dan now immediately departs on road.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet ended he summoned Fan Ze, handed him the edict, and said: "The edict makes you military commissioner. I leave for the capital at once.

sentences.zh: 」因告將吏使謁澤。

translations.literal: Then told officers and clerks to make audience calls on Ze.
translations.idiomatic: He then told his officers and staff to pay their respects to Fan Ze.

sentences.zh: 牙將張獻甫曰：「天子巡幸山南，尚書使行軍奉表起居，而行軍敢自圖節鉞，潛奪尚書土地，此可謂事人不忠。

translations.literal: Ya general Zhang Xianfu said: "Son of Heaven toured south of mountains; Minister sent expeditionary army to present memorial of daily wellbeing; yet expeditionary army dared secretly plot command seal, secretly seize Minister's territory—this can be called serving men without loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The military adjutant Zhang Xianfu said: "The Son of Heaven is on tour in the south. You, Minister, sent General Fan to present your respects—and General Fan dares scheme for the command seal and steal your territory in secret. That is disloyal service.

sentences.zh: 軍中皆不伏，請殺樊澤。

translations.literal: Army all not submit; request to kill Fan Ze.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army refuses to accept this. We ask permission to kill Fan Ze.

sentences.zh: 」耽曰：「公是何言歟！

translations.literal: Dan said: "Sir, what words are these!
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dan said: "What talk is this!

sentences.zh: 天子有命，即為節度使矣。

translations.literal: Son of Heaven has command; then is military commissioner already.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor has spoken—that makes Fan Ze the military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 耽今赴行在，便與公偕行。

translations.literal: Dan now goes to traveling palace; then with you together travel.
translations.idiomatic: I am leaving for the imperial camp now and will travel with you.

sentences.zh: 」即日離鎮，以獻甫自隨，軍中乃安。

translations.literal: Same day left command; took Xianfu along personally; army then settled.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he left his post, taking Zhang Xianfu with him, and the army was pacified.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官為東都留守、東畿汝南防禦使。

translations.literal: Soon with original office as Eastern Capital Protector, Eastern Capital-Ru'nan Defense Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Eastern Capital Protector and Defense Commissioner of the Eastern Capital and Runan regions, retaining his former rank.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，改檢校右僕射、兼滑州刺史、義成軍節度使。

translations.literal: Zhenyuan second year; changed to provisional Right Vice Director, concurrent Huazhou prefect, Yicheng Army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyuan he was made provisional Right Vice Director, prefect of Hua Prefecture, and military commissioner of the Yicheng Army.

sentences.zh: 是時淄青節度使李納雖去偽王號，外奉朝旨，而心常蓄並吞之謀。

translations.literal: At that time Ziqing military commissioner Li Na although removed false king title; outwardly obeyed court edicts; yet heart always harbored annexation schemes.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Na, military commissioner of Ziqing, had renounced his rebel title and outwardly obeyed the court, but he still harbored designs of annexation.

sentences.zh: 納兵士數千人自行營歸，路由滑州，大將請城外館之。

translations.literal: Na's soldiers several thousand from their own camp returning; route passed Huazhou; great generals requested lodging them outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand of Li Na's soldiers were returning from their encampment and passed through Hua Prefecture. His generals asked to quarter them outside the city walls.

sentences.zh: 耽曰：「與人鄰道，奈何野處其兵？

translations.literal: Dan said: "With people neighboring the road; how can wildly lodge their troops?
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dan said: "They are traveling through our neighbor's territory—how can we leave their troops camped in the open?

sentences.zh: 」命館之城內，淄青將士皆心服之。

translations.literal: Ordered lodging within the city walls; Ziqing generals and soldiers all submitted in heart.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that they be quartered inside the city walls, and the generals and soldiers of Ziqing all came to respect him wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 耽善射好獵，每出畋不過百騎，往往獵於李納之境。

translations.literal: Dan excelled at archery and loved hunting; each hunting outing no more than a hundred riders; often hunted in Li Na's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dan was skilled at archery and fond of hunting. Whenever he went out, he took no more than a hundred horsemen, and he often hunted within Li Na's domain.

sentences.zh: 納聞之，大喜，心畏其度量，不敢異圖。

translations.literal: Na heard this; greatly rejoiced; in heart feared his magnanimity; dared not different schemes.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Na heard of this, he was greatly pleased and inwardly feared Jia Dan's magnanimity, and dared not pursue any hostile designs.

sentences.zh: 九年，征為右僕射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Ninth year; summoned as Right Vice Premier, Associate Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenyuan, he was summoned to serve as Right Vice Premier and Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 耽好地理學，凡四夷之使及使四夷還者，必與之從容，訊其山川土地之終始。

translations.literal: Dan loved geography; whenever envoys from the four barbarians or envoys returning from the four barbarians, necessarily with them at leisure inquired of mountains, rivers, and lands from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dan loved the study of geography. Whenever envoys from foreign lands arrived, or whenever envoys returned from missions abroad, he would converse with them at length and inquire about mountains, rivers, and territory in full detail.

sentences.zh: 是以九州之夷險，百蠻之土俗，區分指畫，備究源流。

translations.literal: Thus the nine provinces' level and peril, the hundred barbarians' local customs—distinguished, pointed out, and drawn; fully traced sources and currents.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he distinguished and mapped the terrain of the nine provinces and thoroughly investigated the customs of the hundred foreign peoples, tracing every source and route.

sentences.zh: 自吐蕃陷隴右積年，國家守於內地，舊時鎮戍，不可復知。

translations.literal: Since Tubo captured Longyou for many years, the state guarded the interior lands; old garrison posts could no longer be known.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tibetans had seized Longyou for many years and the state had retreated to the interior, the locations of former frontier garrisons could no longer be known.

sentences.zh: 耽乃畫隴右、山南圖，兼黃河經界遠近，聚其說為書十卷，表獻曰：

translations.literal: Dan then drew maps of Longyou and Shannan, also the Yellow River's boundaries near and far; gathered these accounts into a book of ten scrolls; memorial submitting said:
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dan therefore drew maps of Longyou and the lands south of the mountains, including the Yellow River and the extent of its boundaries near and far. He compiled his findings into a ten-scroll book and submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 臣聞楚左史倚相能讀《九丘》，晉司空裴秀創為六體；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the Chu Left Historian Yi Xiang could read the Nine Mounds, and Jin Minister of Works Pei Xiu created the Six Methods;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Yi Xiang, the left historiographer of Chu, could read the Nine Mounds, and that Pei Xiu, minister of works of Jin, devised the Six Methods of cartography;

sentences.zh: 《九丘》乃成賦之古經，六體則為圖之新意。

translations.literal: The Nine Mounds was an ancient classic for composing fu; the Six Methods were a new conception for maps.
translations.idiomatic: the Nine Mounds was an ancient classic on which fu rhapsodies were composed, while the Six Methods represented a new approach to mapmaking.

sentences.zh: 臣雖愚昧，夙嘗師範，累蒙拔擢，遂忝臺司。

translations.literal: Your servant, though ignorant, from early had teachers and models; repeatedly received elevation; thus undeservingly holds terrace office.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am ignorant, I have studied under worthy teachers from youth, have repeatedly received your favor and promotion, and now undeservedly hold high office at court.

sentences.zh: 雖歷踐職任，誠多曠闕，而率土山川，不忘寤寐。

translations.literal: Although I have passed through offices, truly many neglects and gaps; yet all the land's mountains and rivers—I never forget them waking or sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: Although in my official duties I have indeed fallen short in many ways, I have never ceased to think day and night of the mountains and rivers throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 其大圖外薄四海，內別九州，必藉精詳，乃可摹寫，見更纘集，續冀畢功。

translations.literal: Its great map outward reaches the four seas, inward distinguishes the nine provinces; must rely on minute detail, then can copy and draw; now further gathering and compiling, continue hoping to complete the work.
translations.idiomatic: The great map I envision would reach the four seas without and distinguish the nine provinces within; only with meticulous detail can it be drawn. I am now gathering material further and hope to bring the work to completion.

sentences.zh: 然而隴右一隅，久淪蕃寇，職方失其圖記，境土難以區分。

translations.literal: However Longyou in one corner has long fallen to barbarian raiders; the Directorate of Maps has lost its records; border lands are hard to distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the region of Longyou has long been overrun by barbarian invaders, the Directorate of Maps has lost its records, and its territories can scarcely be distinguished.

sentences.zh: 輒扣課虛微，采掇輿議，畫《關中隴右及山南九州等圖》一軸。

translations.literal: Then examined subtle points, gathered public discussion, and drew one scroll of the Map of Guanzhong, Longyou, and the Nine Provinces of Shannan and Others.
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore investigated every fine point, gathered public testimony, and drawn one scroll entitled Map of Guanzhong, Longyou, and the Nine Provinces South of the Mountains and Other Regions.

sentences.zh: 伏以洮、湟舊墟，連接監牧；

translations.literal: Humbly consider—the old sites of Tao and Huang connect with supervisory pastures;
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully note that the old settlements of the Tao and Huang rivers connect with the frontier pasturelands;

sentences.zh: 甘、涼右地，控帶朔陲。

translations.literal: Gan and Liang, the western lands, control and gird the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: while Gan and Liang, the western territories, command the northern marches.

sentences.zh: 岐路之偵候交通，軍鎮之備禦沖要，莫不匠意就實，依稀像真。

translations.literal: Fork roads' scout routes and communications, military posts' defense of critical points—none not crafted with intent toward reality, vaguely resembling truth.
translations.idiomatic: Scout routes along branching roads, garrison posts guarding strategic points—all have been drawn with painstaking care to match reality as closely as possible.

sentences.zh: 如聖恩遣將護邊，新書授律，則靈、慶之設險在目，原、會之封略可知。

translations.literal: If sagely grace sends generals to guard the borders and new edicts confer regulations, then Ling and Qing's strategic positions are before the eyes, and Yuan and Hui's territorial limits can be known.
