translations.idiomatic: Should Your Majesty send generals to guard the frontier and issue fresh orders, the strategic terrain of Ling and Qing would lie plain before them, and the territorial boundaries of Yuan and Hui would be clear at a glance.

sentences.zh: 諸州諸軍，須論里數人額；

translations.literal: All prefectures and all armies must discuss li counts and personnel quotas;
translations.idiomatic: For every prefecture and every army, the distance in li and the strength of manpower must be set forth;

sentences.zh: 諸山諸水，須言首尾源流。

translations.literal: All mountains and all waters must speak of head and tail, source and flow.
translations.idiomatic: for every mountain and every river, the course from source to mouth must be described.

sentences.zh: 圖上不可備書，憑據必資記註，謹撰《別錄》六卷。

translations.literal: On the map one cannot fully inscribe; reliance must depend on recorded notes; respectfully composed the Separate Record in six scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The map itself cannot contain every detail, so explanatory notes are indispensable. I have therefore respectfully compiled a Separate Record in six scrolls.

sentences.zh: 又黃河為四瀆之宗，西戎乃群羌之帥，臣並研尋史牒，翦棄浮詞，罄所聞知，編為四卷，通錄都成十卷。

translations.literal: Also the Yellow River is chief among the four waterways; Western Rong is leader of the many Qiang tribes; your servant together researched historical records, cut away empty words, exhausted what was heard and known, compiled into four scrolls; altogether with the main record totaling ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River is the greatest of the four sacred rivers, and the Western Rong are the chief of the Qiang peoples. I have also searched the historical records, stripped away empty rhetoric, and set down all I have learned in four additional scrolls, making ten scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 文義鄙樸，伏增慚悚。

translations.literal: Literary meaning rustic and plain; humbly increased shame and awe.
translations.idiomatic: The writing is crude and plain, and I am deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 德宗覽之稱善，賜廄馬一匹、銀采百匹、銀瓶盤各一。

translations.literal: Dezong read it and praised it as good; bestowed one stable horse, one hundred bolts of silver brocade, and one each of silver bottles and dishes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong read the memorial and praised it, bestowing one imperial stable horse, a hundred bolts of silver brocade, and one silver bottle and one silver dish.

sentences.zh: 至十七年，又撰成《海內華夷圖》及《古今郡國縣道四夷述》四十卷，表獻之，曰：

translations.literal: Reaching the seventeenth year, again completed the Map of Chinese and Barbarians Within the Four Seas and the Account of Ancient and Modern Commanderies, Counties, Roads, and the Four Barbarians in forty scrolls; memorial submitting it, saying:
translations.idiomatic: By the seventeenth year of Zhenyuan he had also completed the Map of Chinese and Barbarians Within the Four Seas and the Account of Ancient and Modern Commanderies, Counties, Roads, and the Four Barbarians in forty scrolls, and submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 臣聞地以博厚載物，萬國棋布；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the earth, by its vast thickness, bears all things; the myriad states are laid out like chess pieces;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the earth, in its vast breadth and depth, bears all things, and that the myriad states are spread across it like pieces on a chessboard;

sentences.zh: 海以委輸環外，百蠻繡錯。

translations.literal: The sea, by its winding conveyance, encircles the outer realm; the hundred barbarians are embroidered and interwoven.
translations.idiomatic: that the seas, winding around the outer world, carry all things to and fro, and that the hundred barbarian peoples are interwoven across the land like embroidery.

sentences.zh: 中夏則五服、九州，殊俗則七戎、六狄，普天之下，莫非王臣。

translations.literal: Central Xia has the five domains and nine provinces; foreign customs have the seven Rong and six Di; throughout heaven's beneath, none are not the king's subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Within China lie the five domains and nine provinces; beyond lie the seven Rong and six Di of foreign custom—and under all heaven, none are not the emperor's subjects.

sentences.zh: 昔毋丘出師，東銘不耐；

translations.literal: Formerly Wuqiu marched out with an army; east he inscribed on Mount Bu Nai;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Wuqiu led an army forth and inscribed a stele in the east at Bu Nai;

sentences.zh: 甘英奉使，西抵條支；

translations.literal: Gan Ying was sent on a mission; west he reached Tiaozhi;
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ying was dispatched on a mission and reached Tiaozhi in the west;

sentences.zh: 奄蔡乃大澤無涯，罽賓則懸度作險。

translations.literal: Yancai was a great marsh without bounds; Jibin had the Hanging Crossing as its peril.
translations.idiomatic: Yancai lay by a boundless great marsh, and Jibin was made perilous by the Hanging Crossing.

sentences.zh: 或道理回遠，或名號改移，古來通儒，罕遍詳究。

translations.literal: Some routes were circuitous and distant; some names were changed and shifted; from antiquity learned scholars have rarely fully and thoroughly investigated them all.
translations.idiomatic: Some routes were long and circuitous, and some place names had changed over time; even the most learned scholars of old rarely investigated them fully.

sentences.zh: 臣弱冠之歲，好聞方言，筮仕之辰，註意地理，究觀研考，垂三十年。

translations.literal: In your servant's weak-crown years I loved hearing local dialects; at the divination-of-office time I fixed attention on geography; exhaustively observed and researched, spanning nearly thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: From my youth I loved to hear accounts of foreign lands, and from the time I entered office I devoted myself to geography, studying and investigating the subject for nearly thirty years.

sentences.zh: 絕域之比鄰，異蕃之習俗，梯山獻琛之路，乘舶來朝之人，鹹究竟其源流，訪求其居處。

translations.literal: Neighboring lands of the farthest regions, foreign tribes' customs, roads of climbing mountains to present tribute, people coming to court by ship—all were fully traced to source and current, and their dwelling places sought out.
translations.idiomatic: I traced the origins of neighboring lands beyond the frontier, the customs of foreign peoples, the overland routes by which tribute was carried over mountains, and the seafaring envoys who came to court, and I sought out where they lived.

sentences.zh: 阛阓之行賈，戎貊之遺老，莫不聽其言而掇其要。

translations.literal: Marketplace traveling merchants, frontier old men of Rong and Mo—none not listened to their words and gathered their essentials.
translations.idiomatic: From marketplace traders to old men of the borderlands, I listened to them all and gathered what was essential from their accounts.

sentences.zh: 閭閻之瑣語，風謠之小說，亦收其是而芟其偽。

translations.literal: Neighborhood trivial talk, local songs and minor tales—also gathered what was true and cut away what was false.
translations.idiomatic: Even village gossip and popular songs I sifted, keeping what was sound and discarding what was false.

sentences.zh: 然殷、周以降，封略益明，承歷數者八家，渾區宇者五姓，聲教所及，惟唐為大。

translations.literal: Yet from Yin and Zhou downward, territorial boundaries grew ever clearer; eight houses received the succession; five surnames unified the realm; where civilizing influence reached, only Tang was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the Yin and Zhou dynasties onward territorial boundaries became ever clearer. Eight dynasties received the Mandate, and five ruling houses unified the realm, but in the reach of civilizing influence none surpassed the Tang.

sentences.zh: 秦皇罷侯置守，長城起於臨洮；

translations.literal: The Qin emperor abolished marquisates and established governors; the Long Wall rose from Lintao;
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor of Qin abolished feudal lords and established commandery governors, and the Long Wall began at Lintao;

sentences.zh: 孝武卻地開邊，障塞限於雞鹿；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu pushed back territory and opened the frontier; barrier fortifications were bounded at Jilu;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han expanded the frontier and pushed back the borders, with barrier defenses extending to Jilu;

sentences.zh: 東漢則哀牢請吏；

translations.literal: Eastern Han then had Ailao request officials;
translations.idiomatic: under the Eastern Han, Ailao requested imperial officials;

sentences.zh: 西晉則裨離結轍；

translations.literal: Western Jin then had Bili join in succession;
translations.idiomatic: under the Western Jin, Bili submitted in succession;

sentences.zh: 隋室列四郡於卑和海西，創三州於扶南江北，遼陽失律，因而棄之。

translations.literal: The Sui house established four commanderies west of the Beihe Sea and created three prefectures north of the Funan River; Liaoyang lost discipline and was therefore abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui established four commanderies west of the Beihe Sea and three prefectures north of the Funan River, but when Liaoyang fell out of control those gains were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 高祖神堯皇帝誕膺天命，奄有四方。

translations.literal: Gaozu the Divine Yao Emperor received Heaven's mandate at birth and embraced all four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu, the Divine Yao, received Heaven's mandate and took possession of all four quarters of the realm.

sentences.zh: 太宗繼明重熙，柔遠能邇，逾大磧通道，北至仙娥，於骨利幹置玄闕州。

translations.literal: Taizong succeeded bright glory and doubled radiance; gentle to the distant and able toward the near; crossed the great desert and opened a route; north to Xian'e; at Guligan established Xuanque Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong succeeded him in enlightened rule, winning over distant peoples and governing those nearby. He opened routes across the great desert, reached as far north as Xian'e, and established Xuanque Prefecture among the Guligan.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣守丕績，克廣前烈，遣單車賫詔，西越蔥山，於波刺斯立疾陵府。

translations.literal: Gaozong succeeded and guarded great achievement; able to expand former glory; sent a lone carriage bearing an edict; west crossed Cong Mountain; at Bosi established Jiling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong carried on this great legacy and extended his predecessors' achievements, sending envoys with imperial edicts west beyond the Onion Mountains to establish Jiling Prefecture in Persia.

sentences.zh: 中宗復配天之業，不失舊物。

translations.literal: Zhongzong restored the work of matching Heaven; did not lose the old possessions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong restored the enterprise of matching Heaven and did not lose what had been held before.

sentences.zh: 睿宗含先天之量，惟新永圖。

translations.literal: Ruizong contained the measure of Prior Heaven; only renewed the eternal design.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong possessed the capacity of Prior Heaven and renewed the dynasty's enduring design.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以大孝清內，以無為理外，大宛驥錄，歲充內廄，與貳師之窮兵黷武，豈同年哉！

translations.literal: Xuanzong with great filial piety purified the interior, with non-action governed the exterior; Dayuan's fine horses were recorded, each year filling the inner stables—how could this be comparable to Ershi's exhausting the army and abusing warfare!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong governed the interior through filial devotion and the exterior through effortless rule; the fine horses of Dayuan were registered year after year to fill the imperial stables—surely that was not the same as Li Guangli's ruinous wars of aggression!

sentences.zh: 肅宗掃平氛昆，潤澤生人。

translations.literal: Suzong swept away troubled vapors; moistened and enriched the living people.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong swept away the turmoil and brought relief to the people.

sentences.zh: 代宗刬除殘孽，彜倫攸敘。

translations.literal: Daizong cut away remaining evils; constant norms were thereby ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong eliminated the remaining rebels and restored proper order throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝陛下，以上聖之姿，當太平之運，敦信明義，履信包元，惠養黎蒸，懷柔遐裔。

translations.literal: Humbly consider Your Majesty the Emperor, with supreme sage bearing, meeting the fortune of great peace; thick in faith and bright in righteousness; treading faith and embracing the origin; nourishing and cherishing the black-haired people; cherishing and softening distant tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, in your supreme sagely bearing, has met an age of great peace. You are steadfast in faith and clear in righteousness, cherish and nurture the people, and treat distant peoples with gentle forbearance.

sentences.zh: 故瀘南貢麗水之金，漠北獻余吾之馬，玄化洋溢，率士沾濡。

translations.literal: Therefore south of Lu they presented gold from the Lishui River; north of the desert they offered horses from Yuwu; the dark transforming influence overflowed; all the land was moistened.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the south of Lu presents gold from the Lishui River, and the north of the desert offers horses from Yuwu. Your transforming influence spreads everywhere, and all the land is suffused with its bounty.

sentences.zh: 臣幼切磋於師友，長趨侍於軒墀，自揣孱愚，叨榮非據，鴻私莫答，夙夜兢惶。

translations.literal: Your servant in youth polished himself with teachers and friends; in maturity hastened to attend at the palace steps; estimating myself weak and foolish, undeservedly received glory beyond my station; great favor unanswered; morning and night fearful and reverent.
translations.idiomatic: From youth I studied with teachers and friends, and in maturity I have served at the palace steps. Knowing my own weakness and folly, I am unworthy of the honors I have received and cannot repay your vast kindness; I tremble with awe day and night.

sentences.zh: 去興元元年，伏奉進止，令臣修撰國圖，旋即充使魏州、汴州，出鎮東洛、東都，間以眾務，不遂專門，績用尚虧，憂愧彌切。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan, humbly received orders to have your servant compile the national maps; soon after was dispatched as envoy to Weizhou and Bianzhou, went out to command Eastern Luo and the Eastern Capital; interspersed with many duties, could not devote myself exclusively; achievement still deficient; worry and shame ever keener.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan I received your command to compile a map of the realm, but I was soon sent on missions to Weizhou and Bianzhou and posted to govern Eastern Luo and the Eastern Capital. Other duties intervened, and I could not devote myself fully to the task. The work remains incomplete, and my anxiety and shame grow ever sharper.

sentences.zh: 近乃力竭衰病，思殫所聞見，叢於丹青。

translations.literal: Recently then strength exhausted by decline and illness; thought to exhaust all heard and seen; gathered into red and green.
translations.idiomatic: Now, though my strength is failing with age and illness, I have sought to set down all I have learned and gathered it into this painted map.

sentences.zh: 謹令工人畫《海內華夷圖》一軸，廣三丈，從三丈三尺，率以一寸折成百里。

translations.literal: Respectfully ordered artisans to paint one scroll of the Map of Chinese and Barbarians Within the Four Seas, ten feet wide and thirteen feet long, generally using one inch to represent a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: I have had artisans paint one scroll of the Map of Chinese and Barbarians Within the Four Seas, ten feet wide and thirteen feet long, at a scale of one inch to a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 別章甫左衽，奠高山大川。

translations.literal: Distinguished Chinese cap and left-lapel dress; established high mountains and great rivers.
translations.idiomatic: It distinguishes Chinese from barbarian dress and sets forth the great mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 縮四極於纖縞，分百郡於作繢。

translations.literal: Contracted the four extremities onto fine silk; divided the hundred commanderies in painted rendering.
translations.idiomatic: The four corners of the earth are compressed onto a single silk scroll, and a hundred commanderies are laid out in painted detail.

sentences.zh: 宇宙雖廣，舒之不盈庭；

translations.literal: Though the cosmos is vast, spread out it does not fill a courtyard;
translations.idiomatic: Though the universe is vast, unfolded it fills no more than a courtyard;

sentences.zh: 舟車所通，覽之鹹在目。

translations.literal: Where boats and carts can reach, viewing it all lies before the eyes.
translations.idiomatic: yet every place reachable by boat or cart lies plain before the eye.

sentences.zh: 並撰《古今郡國縣道四夷述》四十卷，中國以《禹貢》為首，外夷以《班史》發源；

translations.literal: Also composed the Account of Ancient and Modern Commanderies, Counties, Roads, and the Four Barbarians in forty scrolls; for China taking the Tribute of Yu as the beginning, for outer barbarians taking the Ban histories as the source;
translations.idiomatic: I have also compiled the Account of Ancient and Modern Commanderies, Counties, Roads, and the Four Barbarians in forty scrolls, beginning the section on China with the Tribute of Yu and the section on foreign lands with the History of the Han by Ban Gu;

sentences.zh: 郡縣紀其增減，蕃落敘其衰盛。

translations.literal: Commanderies and counties record their increases and decreases; barbarian settlements narrate their decline and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: recording the rise and fall of commanderies and counties and the waxing and waning of barbarian settlements.

sentences.zh: 前地理書以黔州屬酉陽，今則改入巴郡；

translations.literal: Earlier geography books placed Qian Prefecture under Youyang; now it is changed to enter Ba Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier geographical works placed Qian Prefecture under Youyang, but it is now assigned to Ba Commandery;

sentences.zh: 前西戎誌以安國為安息，今則改入康居。

translations.literal: Earlier Western Rong records took Anguo as Parthia; now it is changed to enter Kangju;
translations.idiomatic: earlier accounts of the Western Regions treated Anguo as Parthia, but it is now placed under Kangju;

sentences.zh: 凡諸疏舛，悉從厘正。

translations.literal: All such errors and discrepancies were entirely corrected.
translations.idiomatic: and all such errors have been corrected.

sentences.zh: 隴西、十地，播棄於永初之中；

translations.literal: Longxi and the Ten Lands were cast aside in the midst of Yongchu;
translations.idiomatic: Longxi and the Ten Regions were abandoned during the Yongchu era;

sentences.zh: 遼東、樂浪，陷屈於建安之際。

translations.literal: Liaodong and Lelang were encroached upon and reduced at the time of Jian'an;
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong and Lelang were lost during the Jian'an period;

sentences.zh: 曹公棄陘北，晉氏遷江南，緣邊累經侵盜，故墟日致堙毀。

translations.literal: Duke Cao abandoned the north of the passes; the Jin house moved to the lands south of the Yangzi; along the borders repeated invasions and raids occurred; old sites daily fell to burial and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao abandoned the lands north of the passes, the Jin dynasty withdrew south of the Yangzi, and repeated border raids left old sites increasingly buried and ruined.

sentences.zh: 舊史撰錄，十得二三，今書搜補，所獲太半。

translations.literal: Old histories in their compilations recovered two or three parts in ten; the present book through search and supplement obtained more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier histories preserved only two or three parts in ten of this knowledge; in the present work I have recovered more than half through research and supplementation.

sentences.zh: 《周禮職方》，以淄、時為幽州之浸，以華山為荊河之鎮，既有乖於《禹貢》，又不出於淹中，多聞闕疑，詎敢編次。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou's Directorate of Territories takes Zi and Shi as the marshes of Youzhou and Mount Hua as the anchor of Jing and He; this both departs from the Tribute of Yu and does not come from Yanzhong; hearing much yet leaving doubts, how dare I arrange and compile it.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Territories in the Rites of Zhou treats the Zi and Shi rivers as the marshes of Youzhou and Mount Hua as the landmark of Jing and He. This both conflicts with the Tribute of Yu and cannot be traced to the archives of Qi. Where much is heard but doubtful, I dare not set it down in order.

sentences.zh: 其古郡國題以墨，今州縣題以硃，今古殊文，執習簡易。

translations.literal: Ancient commanderies and states are titled in black ink; present prefectures and counties are titled in vermilion; present and ancient have different script; holding and learning are simple and easy.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient commanderies and kingdoms are labeled in black ink and present prefectures and counties in vermilion, so that past and present are distinct and the map is easy to read.

sentences.zh: 臣學謝小成，才非博物。

translations.literal: Your servant's learning falls short of minor completion; talent is not that of broad knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: My learning is far from complete, and my talent falls short of true erudition.

sentences.zh: 伏波之聚米，開示眾軍；

translations.literal: Fubo's gathering of rice grains opened and showed the host of armies;
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Yuan piled rice to model the terrain, he showed the whole army what lay ahead;

sentences.zh: 酂侯之圖書，方知厄塞。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Pei's maps and records—only then knew the passes and blockages.
translations.idiomatic: and when Xiao He preserved the maps and records, the strategic passes became known.

sentences.zh: 企慕前哲，嘗所寄心，輒罄庸陋，多慚紕繆。

translations.literal: Looking up in admiration to former sages was what I ever entrusted my heart to; then exhausted my mediocrity and vulgarity; much ashamed of errors and slips.
translations.idiomatic: I have long admired these earlier sages and poured my heart into this work, but I have exhausted my humble abilities and fear there are many errors.

sentences.zh: 優詔答之，賜錦彩二百匹、袍段六、錦帳二、銀瓶盤各一、銀榼二、馬一匹，進封魏國公。

translations.literal: An excellent edict answered him; bestowed two hundred bolts of brocade, six robe lengths, two brocade tents, one each of silver bottles and dishes, two silver flasks, one horse; advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with a gracious edict and bestowed two hundred bolts of brocade, six lengths of robe silk, two brocade tents, one silver bottle and one silver dish, two silver flasks, and one horse, promoting him to Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，檢校司空，守左僕射，知政事如故。

translations.literal: When Shunzong acceded; provisional Minister of Works; held Left Vice Premier; managed state affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong acceded to the throne, Jia Dan was made provisional Minister of Works and retained his post as Left Vice Premier, continuing to manage state affairs as before.

sentences.zh: 時王叔文用事，政出群小，耽惡其亂政，屢移病乞骸，不許。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Shuwen held power; government issued from a clique of petty men; Dan hated their disorderly governance; repeatedly submitted illness pleading to retire; not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Shuwen held power and policy was dictated by a clique of petty officials. Jia Dan detested their corrupt governance and repeatedly pleaded illness to retire, but was not permitted to do so.

sentences.zh: 耽性長者，不喜臧否人物。

translations.literal: Dan's nature was that of a gentleman of mature virtue; he did not like to judge people good or bad.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dan was by nature a man of mature virtue and did not care to pass judgment on others.

sentences.zh: 自居相位，凡十三年，雖不能以安危大計啟沃於人主，而常以檢身厲行以律人。

translations.literal: From occupying the chief minister's seat, altogether thirteen years; although unable with security-and-danger great plans to nourish and enrich the sovereign, yet always used examining himself and strict conduct to regulate others.
translations.idiomatic: During the thirteen years he served as chief minister, he may not have offered the emperor far-reaching counsel on matters of national security, but he always disciplined himself strictly and thereby set an example for others.

sentences.zh: 每自朝歸第，接對賓客，終日無倦。

translations.literal: Each time returning from court to his residence, receiving and answering guests, all day without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he returned home from court, he received guests and conversed with them tirelessly throughout the day.

sentences.zh: 至於家人近習，未嘗見其喜慍之色，古之淳德君子，何以加焉！

translations.literal: As for family members and close attendants, they never saw his pleased or angry expression; the pure-virtue gentlemen of antiquity—how could one add to that!
translations.idiomatic: Even his family and close attendants never saw him show pleasure or anger. What more could be asked of the pure-hearted gentlemen of old!

sentences.zh: 永貞元年十月卒，時年七十六。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongzhen he died; at the time age seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of the first year of Yongzhen, at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 廢朝四日，冊贈太傅，謚曰元靖。

translations.literal: Court mourning was suspended four days; by edict posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor; posthumous title Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Court audiences were suspended for four days. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Yuanjing, "Originally Tranquil."

sentences.zh: 姜公輔姜公輔，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Jiang Gongfu—Jiang Gongfu; not known from what place.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gongfu—his place of origin is unknown.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，為校書郎。

translations.literal: Passed the jinshi examination; served as Collator.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed collator.

sentences.zh: 應制策科高等，授左拾遺，召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: Responded to the imperial policy examination with high rank; appointed Left Reminder; summoned into the Hanlin Academy as academician.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked high in the imperial policy examination, was appointed Left Reminder, and was summoned to serve as a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 歲滿當改官，公輔上書自陳，以母老家貧，以府掾俸給稍優，乃求兼京兆尹戶曹參軍，特承恩顧。

translations.literal: When his term expired he should have changed office; Gongfu submitted a memorial stating himself; because his mother was old and his family poor; because the prefectural aide's salary was somewhat better; then requested concurrently Capital Intendant's Household Affairs Administrator; specially received imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired and he was due for a new appointment, Jiang Gongfu submitted a memorial explaining that his mother was elderly and his family poor, and that the salary of a prefectural aide was somewhat better. He therefore requested the concurrent post of household affairs administrator under the capital intendant and received special imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 才高有器識，每對見言事，德宗多從之。

translations.literal: Talent high with capacity and insight; each time in audience speaking on affairs; Dezong mostly followed him.
translations.idiomatic: He was talented and far-sighted, and whenever he spoke on affairs in audience Emperor Dezong usually followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 建中四年十月，涇師犯闕。

translations.literal: Jianzhong fourth year tenth month; Jingzhou troops violated the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Jianzhong, the Jingzhou troops rebelled and attacked the capital.

sentences.zh: 德宗蒼黃自苑北便門出幸，公輔馬前諫曰：「硃泚嘗為涇原帥，得士心。

translations.literal: Dezong in panic from the northern convenience gate of the park departed on tour; Gongfu before his horse remonstrated saying: "Zhu Ci once was Jingyuan commander; won soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong fled in panic through the northern side gate of the imperial park. Jiang Gongfu rode ahead of him and remonstrated: "Zhu Ci once commanded Jingyuan and won the loyalty of his troops.

sentences.zh: 昨以硃滔叛，坐奪兵權，泚常憂憤不得誌。

translations.literal: Yesterday because Zhu Tao rebelled, he sat and had military authority taken away; Ci constantly grieved and resented, unable to fulfill his ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Because his brother Zhu Tao rebelled, he was stripped of command, and Zhu Ci has long brooded in anger and frustration.

sentences.zh: 不如使人捕之，使陪鑾駕，忽群兇立之，必貽國患。

translations.literal: Better to send men to arrest him and have him accompany the imperial carriage; if suddenly the evil clique installs him, surely will leave a national calamity.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to have him arrested, or at least to have him accompany the imperial carriage. If the rebels suddenly set him up as leader, it will bring disaster upon the state.

sentences.zh: 臣頃曾陳奏，陛下茍不能坦懷待之，則殺之，養獸自貽其患，悔且無益。

translations.literal: Your servant recently once submitted memorial; if Your Majesty cannot with open heart treat him, then kill him; raising a beast oneself brings its calamity; regret will be without benefit.
translations.idiomatic: I recently memorialized on this matter. If Your Majesty cannot treat him with open sincerity, then kill him. To keep a dangerous beast is to invite disaster; regret will come too late.

sentences.zh: 」德宗曰：「已無及矣！

translations.literal: Dezong said: "Already too late!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong said: "It is already too late!

sentences.zh: 」從幸至奉天，拜諫議大夫，俄以本官同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Accompanied the imperial tour to Fengtian; appointed Remonstrance and Counsel Grand Master; soon with his original office made Associate Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Fengtian, was appointed Remonstrance and Counsel Grand Master, and soon thereafter was made Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery while retaining that post.

sentences.zh: 從幸山南，車駕至城固縣，唐安公主薨。

translations.literal: Accompanied the imperial tour to Shannan; the imperial carriage reached Chenggu County; Princess Tang'an died.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled south to Shannan and the imperial procession reached Chenggu County, Princess Tang'an died.

sentences.zh: 上之長女，昭德皇后所生，性聰敏仁孝，上所鐘愛。

translations.literal: The emperor's eldest daughter; born of Empress Zhaode; nature intelligent, perceptive, benevolent, and filial; the emperor deeply cherished her.
translations.idiomatic: She was the emperor's eldest daughter, born to Empress Zhaode. Intelligent, benevolent, and filial by nature, she was deeply beloved by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 初，詔尚韋宥，未克禮會而遇播遷；

translations.literal: Initially an edict betrothed her to Wei You; had not been able to complete the rites when they encountered forced relocation;
translations.idiomatic: An edict had betrothed her to Wei You, but the marriage rites had not yet been performed when the court was forced to flee;

sentences.zh: 及薨，上悲悼尤甚，詔所司厚其葬禮。

translations.literal: When she died, the emperor grieved and mourned her especially deeply and ordered the relevant offices to make her funeral rites lavish.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, the emperor grieved deeply and ordered the responsible offices to give her a lavish funeral.

sentences.zh: 公輔諫曰：「非久克復京城，公主必須歸葬，今於行路，且宜儉薄，以濟軍士。

translations.literal: Gongfu remonstrated, saying: "Before long the capital will be recovered; the princess must be returned for burial there. For now, on the road, the rites should be kept frugal to aid the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu remonstrated, "The capital will soon be recovered and the princess must be buried there. For now, on campaign, the rites should be kept frugal so resources may aid the troops.

sentences.zh: 」德宗怒，謂翰林學士陸贄曰：「唐安夭亡，不欲於此為塋壟，宜令造一磚塔安置，功費甚微，不合關宰相論列。

translations.literal: " Emperor Dezong was angry and said to Hanlin Academician Lu Zhi: "Tang'an died young; I do not wish to make a tomb mound here. She should be placed in a brick pagoda; the labor cost is very slight and ought not to concern the chief ministers in debate.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Dezong was angry and told Hanlin academician Lu Zhi, "Tang'an died young; I do not wish to raise a tomb here. Let a brick pagoda be built for her—the cost is trifling and should not be a matter for the chief ministers to debate.

sentences.zh: 姜公輔忽進表章，都無道理，但欲指朕過失，擬自取名。

translations.literal: Jiang Gongfu suddenly submitted a memorial wholly without reason, intending only to point out my faults and make a name for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gongfu suddenly submitted a memorial wholly without reason, intending only to point out my faults and win a reputation for himself.

sentences.zh: 朕比擢拔為腹心，乃負朕如此！

translations.literal: I recently promoted him as a trusted intimate, yet he has betrayed me thus!
translations.idiomatic: I recently promoted him as a trusted confidant, yet he has betrayed me like this!

sentences.zh: 」贄對曰：「公輔官是諫議，職居宰衡，獻替固其職分。

translations.literal: " Lu Zhi replied: "Gongfu's office is remonstrance; his duty stands among the chief ministers; offering correction is indeed his proper charge.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Zhi replied, "Gongfu holds a remonstrance office and ranks among the chief ministers; offering correction is his proper duty.

sentences.zh: 本立輔臣，置之左右，朝夕納誨，意在防微，微而弼之，乃其所也。

translations.literal: Assistants are established and placed at one's side to offer counsel morning and evening; the intent is to guard against the slightest fault, and to assist when faults are slight—that is their role.
translations.idiomatic: Assistants are placed at the ruler's side to offer counsel morning and evening; their purpose is to guard against the slightest fault and to assist when faults are slight—that is their role.

sentences.zh: 陛下以造塔役費微小，非宰相所論之事。

translations.literal: Your Majesty holds that building the pagoda costs little labor and is not a matter for the chief ministers to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty holds that building the pagoda costs little and is not a matter for the chief ministers to discuss.

sentences.zh: 但問理之是非，豈論事之大小！

translations.literal: One should ask only whether the principle is right or wrong—how can one judge by the size of the affair!
translations.idiomatic: One should ask only whether the principle is right or wrong—how can one judge by the size of the matter!

sentences.zh: 若造塔為是，役雖大而作之何傷！

translations.literal: If building the pagoda is right, even if the labor is great, what harm in doing it!
translations.idiomatic: If building the pagoda is right, even if the labor is great, what harm is there in doing it!

sentences.zh: 若造塔為非，費雖小而言者何罪！

translations.literal: If building the pagoda is wrong, even if the cost is small, what crime has the speaker committed!
translations.idiomatic: If building the pagoda is wrong, even if the cost is small, what crime has the remonstrator committed!

sentences.zh: 」帝又曰：「卿未會朕意。

translations.literal: " The emperor also said: "You have not grasped my intent.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor also said, "You have not grasped my intent.

sentences.zh: 朕以公輔才行，共宰相都不相當，在奉天時已欲罷免，後因公輔辭退，朕已面許。

translations.literal: I consider Gongfu's talent and conduct quite unequal to that of the chief ministers together; at Fengtian I already wished to remove him, and later, because Gongfu asked to resign, I already promised him to his face.
translations.idiomatic: I consider Gongfu's talent and conduct quite unequal to the chief ministers as a group; at Fengtian I already wished to remove him, and later, when he asked to resign, I promised him to his face.

sentences.zh: 尋屬懷光背叛，遂且因循，容至山南。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Huai'guang rebelled, so I deferred the matter for the time being and allowed him to reach Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Huai'guang rebelled, so I deferred the matter and allowed him to remain in Shannan.

sentences.zh: 公輔知朕擬改官，所以固論造塔，賣直取名。

translations.literal: Gongfu knew I planned to change his office, so he obstinately argued about building the pagoda, selling uprightness to win a name.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu knew I planned to change his post, so he obstinately argued about the pagoda, peddling blunt honesty to win a reputation.

sentences.zh: 據此用心，豈是良善！

translations.literal: Judging by this intent, how can he be good!
translations.idiomatic: Judging by this intent, how can he be called good!

sentences.zh: 朕所惆悵者，只緣如此。

translations.literal: What I find vexing is precisely this.
translations.idiomatic: What troubles me is precisely this.

sentences.zh: 」贄再三救護，帝怒不已，乃罷為左庶子。

translations.literal: " Lu Zhi repeatedly tried to shield him, but the emperor's anger did not cease, and Gongfu was dismissed to Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Zhi repeatedly tried to shield him, but the emperor's anger did not abate, and Gongfu was demoted to left guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂，服闕，授右庶子，久之不遷。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother; when mourning ended he was appointed Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and for a long time received no further promotion.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered mourning for his mother; when mourning ended he was appointed right guardian of the heir apparent and for a long time received no further promotion.

sentences.zh: 洎陸贄知政事，以有翰林之舊，數告贄求官。

translations.literal: When Lu Zhi directed state affairs, because of their old ties in the Hanlin Academy, Gongfu repeatedly told Zhi he sought an office.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Zhi directed state affairs, Gongfu, citing their old ties in the Hanlin Academy, repeatedly asked Zhi for promotion.

sentences.zh: 贄密謂公輔曰：「予嘗見郴州竇相，言為公奏擬數矣，上旨不允，有怒公之言。

translations.literal: Zhi secretly told Gongfu: "I once saw Chief Minister Dou at Chenzhou; he said he had submitted several nominations for you, but the imperial intent did not approve, and there were words of anger toward you.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi secretly told Gongfu, "I once saw Chief Minister Dou at Chenzhou; he said he had submitted several nominations for you, but the throne did not approve, and the emperor spoke angrily of you.

sentences.zh: 」公輔恐懼，上疏乞罷官為道士，久之未報。

translations.literal: " Gongfu was afraid and submitted a memorial asking to resign his office and become a Daoist priest; for a long time there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Gongfu was frightened and submitted a memorial asking to resign and become a Daoist priest; for a long time there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 後又廷奏，德宗問其故，公輔不敢泄贄，便以參言為對。

translations.literal: Later he again presented at court; Dezong asked the reason, and Gongfu, not daring to reveal Zhi, answered with Dou's words.
translations.idiomatic: He later presented again at court; Dezong asked the reason, and Gongfu, not daring to implicate Zhi, answered with Dou's words.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，貶公輔為泉州別駕，又遣中使賫詔責竇參。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, demoted Gongfu to Assistant Prefect of Quanzhou, and also sent a palace envoy bearing an edict to rebuke Dou Can.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry, demoted Gongfu to assistant prefect of Quanzhou, and also sent a palace envoy with an edict rebuking Dou Can.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，起為吉州刺史，尋卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong ascended the throne, Gongfu was recalled as Prefect of Jizhou and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong ascended the throne, Gongfu was recalled as prefect of Jizhou and soon died.

sentences.zh: 憲宗朝，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xianzong he was posthumously given Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzong he was posthumously made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：賈魏公以溫克長者，致位丞相，拒獻甫之請，畋李納之郊，則器略可知矣！

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Duke Jia of Wei, as a gentle and self-restrained elder, rose to chief minister; he refused Xianfu's request and hunted in Li Na's borderlands—his capacity and breadth of view may thus be known!
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Duke Jia of Wei, a gentle and self-restrained elder, rose to chief minister; he refused Xianfu's plea and hunted on Li Na's borders—his breadth of character may thus be known!

sentences.zh: 韋郢公慷慨節義，困於讒邪，命矣夫！

translations.literal: Duke Wei of Ying was generous in spirit and firm in integrity, yet trapped by slander and wickedness—such was his fate!
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wei of Ying was generous in spirit and firm in integrity, yet trapped by slander and wickedness—such was his fate!

sentences.zh: 趙丞相區分檢裁，求為雅士，以爭權而陷陸贄，則前時以德報怨，其可信乎！

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhao distinguished and examined affairs, seeking to be a refined gentleman; yet by struggling for power he brought down Lu Zhi—then his earlier repaying enmity with virtue, can it be believed!
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhao distinguished affairs carefully and sought to be a refined gentleman; yet by struggling for power he brought down Lu Zhi—so can his earlier claim to repay enmity with virtue be believed!

sentences.zh: 公輔一言悟主，驟及臺司；

translations.literal: Gongfu with one word moved his ruler and suddenly reached the highest offices;
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu with one word moved his ruler and suddenly reached the highest offices;

sentences.zh: 一言不合，禮遽疏薄，則加膝墜泉之間，君道可知矣！

translations.literal: with one word out of accord, favor was suddenly withdrawn and treatment grew thin—between drawing one to the knee and casting one into the abyss, the way of a ruler may thus be known!
translations.idiomatic: with one word out of accord, favor was suddenly withdrawn—the distance between drawing a man to one's knee and casting him into the abyss shows how the way of rulership may be known!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：元靖訏謨，真謂純儒。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Yuanjing's far-reaching plans—he may truly be called a pure Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Yuanjing's far-reaching counsel—he may truly be called a pure Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: 手調鼎飪，心運地圖。

translations.literal: With his hand he adjusted the cauldron and stew; with his mind he moved the maps.
translations.idiomatic: With his hand he seasoned the state's stew; with his mind he charted the realm.

sentences.zh: 姜躁趙險，並躍天衢。

translations.literal: Jiang was impetuous, Zhao was perilous—both leaped upon the heavenly highway.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was impetuous, Zhao was perilous—both vaulted onto the road to high office.

sentences.zh: 哀哉韋公，終困讒夫。

translations.literal: Alas for Duke Wei—he was ultimately trapped by slanderers.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for Duke Wei—he was ultimately undone by slanderers.
